sites.name: The Tropical Atlantic Region
sites.context: The Tropical Atlantic Region covers both sides of the Atlantic Ocean.

sites.name: Terra firma
sites.context: Terra firma literally means “firm earth,” and refers to rainforest that is not inundated by flooded rivers.

sites.name: The lower Congo
sites.context: The lower Congo comprises the lower section of the main river from its mouth at the Atlantic Ocean to the twin capitals of Brazzaville and Kinshasha.

sites.name: The Mano River
sites.context: The Mano River is located in northern Liberia and southeastern Guinea.

sites.name: Luzon
sites.context: Luzon is located in the northern Philippines, and is the largest and by far the most populous of the islands.

sites.name: Lowland rainforests
sites.context: Lowland rainforests occupy a relatively narrow strip between the eastern coast and the mountainous Central Highlands, from sea level to 800 metres elevation.

sites.name: The South China Sea
sites.context: The South China Sea is located south of China, east of Vietnam, the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, west of the Philippines, and north of Borneo.

sites.name: The Sierra Madre del Sur
sites.context: The Sierra Madre del Sur is located in southwestern Mexico, extending 1,000 kilometres from southern Michoacán and east through Guerrero to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec in eastern Oaxaca.

sites.name: The Gulf of Guinea
sites.context: The Gulf of Guinea is located in the eastern tropical Atlantic on the western coast of Africa, extending from Cape Palmas in Liberia south to Cape Lopez in Gabon.

sites.name: Scattered patches of lowland dry forest
sites.context: Scattered patches of lowland dry forest still remain in eastern Mexico on the northern tip of the Yucatán Peninsula as well as in a small area of east-cental coastal Mexico and much of the southwestern and southern Mexican Pacific coast.

sites.name: The Sierra Madre de Oaxaca
sites.context: The Sierra Madre de Oaxaca is located in south-central Mexico, primarily in the state of Oaxaca but also including parts of eastern Puebla and western Veracruz.

sites.name: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
sites.context: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts, are located on the South Atlantic Ridge in the South Atlantic Ocean.

sites.name: The East African coastal forests
sites.context: The East African coastal forests are a tropical moist forest region located in a narrow band along the Indian Ocean coast from southern Somalia in the north, through coastal Kenya and Tanzania to just north of the mouth of the Limpopo River in southern Mozambique.

sites.name: The Cape Verde Rise
sites.context: The Cape Verde Rise is an oceanic feature that includes the Cape Verde Islands and other islands west of the African continental shelf.

sites.name: The Sala y Gómez Ridge
sites.context: The Sala y Gómez Ridge is a mostly submarine mountain range located in the eastern South Pacific.

sites.name: The Western Indo-Pacific
sites.context: The Western Indo-Pacific comprises the tropical waters of the western and central Indian Ocean.

sites.name: The Cordillera Central
sites.context: The Cordillera Central is a large mountain range located in north-central Luzon.

sites.name: The Red Sea
sites.context: The Red Sea is a seawater inlet of the Indian Ocean lying between Africa and Asia.

sites.name: The Luapula River
sites.context: The Luapula River is a transitional river forming, for nearly all of its length, part of the border between Zambia and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

sites.name: The South Atlantic Ridge
sites.context: The South Atlantic Ridge is the southern part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, which runs along the floor of the Atlantic Ocean through both the northern and southern hemispheres.

sites.name: The Chagos-Laccadive Ridge
sites.context: The Chagos-Laccadive Ridge is a vast volcanic ridge and oceanic plateau extending between the northern and central Indian Ocean.

sites.name: The Ituri / Aruwimi River
sites.context: The Ituri / Aruwimi River is located in northeastern and north-central Democratic Republic of Congo.

sites.name: Espiritu Santo
sites.context: Espiritu Santo is the largest of the Vanuatu Islands.

sites.name: The cerrado
sites.context: The cerrado is a vast and biologically rich tropical savanna and woodland region of east-central and southeastern Brazil, eastern and central Bolivia, and eastern Paraguay.

sites.name: Palawan
sites.context: Palawan is a long, narrow island located in the southwestern Philippines.

sites.name: The Albertine Rift
sites.context: The Albertine Rift is the western branch of the East African Rift and covers parts of Uganda, Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda, Burundi, and western Tanzania.

sites.name: The Lufira River
sites.context: The Lufira River is located in south-central and southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

sites.name: The Isthmian Highlands
sites.context: The Isthmian Highlands is the name given for the chain of mountains extending from southeastern Nicaragua to west-central Panama.

sites.name: The Bay of Bengal
sites.context: The Bay of Bengal is located in the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean.

sites.name: The Norfolk Ridge
sites.context: The Norfolk Ridge is a long, mostly submarine ridge running between New Caledonia and New Zealand, about 1,300 kilometres off the eastern coast of Australia.

sites.name: The Kyushu-Palau Ridge
sites.context: The Kyushu-Palau Ridge is an extinct volcanic line on the seafloor that runs from the Japanese island of Kyushu southeast to Palau.

sites.name: Miombo
sites.context: “Miombo” is the vernacular word for Brachystegia, a genus of tree comprising a large number of species notable for shedding their leaves during the dry season.

sites.name: Negros
sites.context: Negros is a relatively large, mountainous island located in the central Philippines.

sites.name: Manus
sites.context: Manus is the largest of the Admiralty Islands and, unlike the other islands in its group, still retains much of its original rainforest cover.

sites.name: The Luhoho River
sites.context: The Luhoho River is located in central-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

sites.name: The Nyong River
sites.context: The Nyong River is located in southwestern Cameroon.

sites.name: The Sanaga River
sites.context: The Sanaga River is located in western and central Cameroon.

sites.name: The Sierra Nevada de Mérida
sites.context: The Sierra Nevada de Mérida is located in Mérida and Barinas states.

sites.name: Mindanao
sites.context: Located in the southeastern Philippines, Mindanao is the second largest island in the archipelago.

sites.name: The Flores Sea
sites.context: The Flores Sea is located south of Sulawesi and north of Flores and Sumbawa in the Lesser Sunda Islands.

sites.name: The North Atlantic Ridge
sites.context: The North Atlantic Ridge is the northern part of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, the longest mountain range in the world, extending as it does almost discontinuously through the northern and southern hemispheres.

sites.name: Arrowsmith Bank
sites.context: Arrowsmith Bank is a wholly submerged bank located off the northeastern tip of the Yucatán Peninsula, Mexico.

The Morelia killifish (Anablepsoides taeniatus) is known only from the upper Caquetá River drainage of southwestern Colombia, where it was last collected during the 1940s.
The Marañón dwarf cichlid (Apistogramma rositae) is known only from the Marañon River drainage between the Pastaza and Tigre tributaries, opposite the mouth of the Huallaga River (Loreto department).
Boulenger's naked suckermouth catfish (Astroblepus boulengeri) is confined to the Napo-Pastaza drainage in eastern Ecuador.
The Khwae Noi naked catfish (Batasio tigrinus) and Khwae Noi torrent catfish (Amblyceps variegatum) are both known only from hillstreams within the Khwae Noi River drainage.
The Seetha danio (Betadevario ramachandrani) is confined to the upper Seetha River drainage.
species.iucn: Betadevario ramachandrani Pramod, Fang, Rema Devi, Liao, Indra, Jameela Beevi & Kullander, 2010

species.e: The Rio Grande sucker (Catostomus plebeius) is confined to the Rio Grande drainage.
Elias' characin (Chrysobrycon eliasi) is known only from the Madre de Dios River drainage in southeastern Peru.
The scarlet chameleonfish (Dario dario) is known only from tributary streams in the Brahmaputra drainage of northern India (West Bengal and Assam), though it may perhaps occur as well in Bhutan.
The Leuk danio (Devario acrostomus) is known only from forested streams within the Leuk River drainage.
Lang's disichodus (Distichodus langi) is known only from Faradje in the Uele River drainage.
Wellman's barbel (Enteromius wellmani) is confined to the upper reaches of the Cuvo River drainage.
Buchanan's mountain catfish (Glyptothorax buchanani) is known only from the upper Chao Phraya River drainage.
The Sierra del Divisor characin (Hemibrycon divisorensis) is known only from the right margin of the Ucayali River drainage in Peru.
species.iucn: Hemibrycon divisorensis Bertaco, Malabarba, Hidalgo & Ortega, 2007

species.e: The Chintadó characin (Hemibrycon microformaa) is known only from the upper Atrato River drainage.
The Páez characin (Hemibrycon paez) is known only from the Páez River drainage.
The La Miel characin (Hemibrycon raqueliae) is confined to creeks within the La Miel River drainage.
The rhinoceros yellowfish (Labeobarbus rhinoceros) is confined to the Athi and Tana River drainage in Kenya, where it is heavily fished.
The ornate catfish (Nangra ornata) is known only from the Surma-Meghna drainage in northeastern Bangladesh (Sylhet province).
The Pegu stone loach (Neonoemacheilus peguensis) is known only from the Pegu Range.
Barton's cichlid (Nosferatu bartoni) is confined to a few areas of the Pánuco River drainage.
The Mae Sa Nga bat-catfish (Oreoglanis laciniosus) is known only from two streams in the Mae Sa Nga drainage.
Ahl's catfish (Parauchenoglanis ahli) is known only from the upper Cross River drainage.
The Dê catfish (Pareuchiloglanis namdeensis) is known only from the Dê River drainage.

The ruby barb (Pethia padamya) is a popular aquarium fish that, in the wild state, is known only from the lower Irrawaddy drainage along with an artificial pond above the Anisakan Falls in central Myanmar.
Teugels' bichir (Polypterus teugelsi) is known only from the upper Cross River drainage.
The Oman dottyback (Pseudochromis omanensis) is known only from coastal Oman and the Socotra Archipelago.
The Da Rang bumblebee catfish (Pseudomystus sobrinus) is known only from the Da Rang River drainage.
Rusby's three-barbeled catfish (Rhamdella rusbyi) is known only from the upper Beni River drainage.
The Lam stream goby (Rhinogobius nganfoensis) is confined to creeks and small rivers within the catchment area of the Lam River in northern Vietnam (Nghe An province).
The Dong Nai stone loach (Schistura dalatensis) is known only from the Dong Nai River drainage.
The Ping stone loach (Schistura spilota) is confined to the upper Ping River drainage.
The Tibetan osman (Schizopygopsis thermalis) is confined to the upper Salween River drainage in Tibet.
The blunt-nosed snowtrout (Schizothorax molesworthi) is known only from the upper Brahmaputra River drainage, where it is heavily exploited for food.
The Caquetá whiptail catfish (Spatuloricaria euacanthagenys) is known only from the upper Caquetá River drainage of southwestern Colombia.
The Ngoi Bo catfish (Tachysurus longispinalis) is known only from the Ngoi Bo River drainage.
The long-finned loach (Yasuhikotakia longidorsalis) is confined to the Mekong drainage of central Laos and northeastern Thailand, where it is threatened by dam construction.
The McIlwraith rainforest frog (Cophixalus peninsularis) is known only from the McIlwraith Range.
The Sira rocket frog (Hyloxalus patitae) is confined to the Sira Range.
The Bocaina robber frog (Ischnocnema pusilla) is known only from the Bocaina Range.
The grey swamp frog (Papurana grisea) is known only from the Went Range.

The San Luis beaked toad (Rhinella sclerocephala) is confined to the San Luis Range, where it is threatened by loss of habitat and overcollection for use in “traditional medicine.” Neild's leaf frog (Phyllomedusa neildi) appears to be confined to the San Luis Range.
The Guaratuba foam-nest frog (Physalaemus insperatus) is known only from the Pedra Branca do Araraquara Range.
The Cariri foam-nest frog (Physalaemus irroratus) is known only from the Cariri Range.
The Tapirapecó carrying frog (Stefania tamacuarina) is known only from the Tapirapecó Range.
The Tembagapura fanged frog (Xenorhina adisca) is known only from the Sudirman Range.
The white-chinned myzomela (Myzomela albigula) is a type of honeyeater known only from the smaller islands of the Louisiade Archipelago.
Budin's chinchilla rat (Abrocoma budini) appears to be confined to the Ambato Range.
The Famatina chinchilla rat (Abrocoma famatina) is known only from the Famatina Range.
The Uspallata chinchilla rat (Abrocoma uspallata) is known only from two localities within the Uspallata Range.
Wolffsohn's viscacha (Lagidium wolffsohni) is a chinchilla-like rodent confined to the Baguales Range.
Duellman's anole (Anolis duellmani) is confined to the Tuxtlas Range.
The Juárez anole (Anolis rubiginosus) is confined to the Juárez Range.
The Pirre galliwasp (Diploglossus montisilvestris) is a type of lizard confined to the Pirre Range.
The Macarena snail-eater (Dipsas baliomelas) is a type of snake known only from cloud forests in the Macarena Range.
The Coalcomán earth snake (Geophis incomptus) is confined to an area of the Coalcomán Range in Jalisco.
The Pirre blunt-headed vine snake (Imantodes phantasma) is confined to the Pirre Range.
Liner's tropical night lizard (Lepidophyma lineri) is confined to the Miahuatlán Range.
The Aconquija tree iguana (Liolaemus griseus) is known only from a small area of the Aconquija Range.
The Juárez graceful brown snake (Rhadinaea bogertorum) is known only from a small area of the Juárez Range.
The pricklefish (Abyssoberyx levisquamosus) is known only from a few specimens collected from deep waters off northwestern Africa.
The thornbush blenny (Acanthemblemaria harpeza) is known only from two, widely-spaced localities (Navassa Island and St.
The Brazilian seabass (Acanthistius brasilianus) is a rare species confined to the coastal waters of southern Brazil.
The New Caledonian seabream (Acanthopagrus akazakii) is known only from specimens collected off Grande Terre, New Caledonia.
The Bengal yellowfin seabream (Acanthopagrus longispinnis) is known only from two localities in the northwestern Bay of Bengal.
The black-margined seabream (Acanthopagrus omanensis) is known only from a few specimens and observations from the coast of central Oman.
species.iucn: Acanthopagrus omanensis Iwatsuki & Heemstra, in press

species.e: The Middle East black seabream (Acanthopagrus randalli) is known only from two specimens collected in the Persian Gulf and a photo taken off the coast of southwestern Pakistan.
The southern little pipehorse (Acentronura australe) is known only from a few specimens collected in disjunct seagrass areas of southern and western Australia.
The anomalous characin (Acestrocephalus anomalus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the middle and lower Magdalena-Cauca drainage.
Deignan's bitterling (Acheilognathus deignani) is confined to a few small tributaries in northwestern Laos and northwestern Vietnam, where it is threatened by loss of habitat and overfishing.
The Nho Que barb (Acrossocheilus baolacensis) is confined to the Nho Que River.
The Chu barb (Acrossocheilus xamensis) is known only from two specimens collected from the Chu River in northeastern Laos (Louangphrabang province).
The shortfin mini dartfish (Aioliops brachypterus) is known only from coral reefs off Miniloc and El Nido in the western Philippines.
The Atlantic specter goby (Akko dionaea) is known only from the mouth of the Amazon River, along with some larval forms recorded from off the coast of northern Colombia.
The Tenasserim stream catfish (Akysis pictus) is confined to southern peninsular Myanmar.
The Arakan stream catfish (Akysis vespertinus) is known only from the western face of the Arakan Mountains in south-central Myanmar.
Springer's shore-eel (Alabes springeri) is known only from the shallow waters around Norfolk Island.
The Korean bonefish (Albula koreana) is known only from a few specimens collected along the southeastern coast of the Korean Peninsula and the northern coast of Taiwan.
The longjaw bonefish (Albula virgata) is confined to shallow sandflats in the Hawaiian Islands.
The western Indo-Pacific toadfish (Allenbatrachus meridionalis) is a freshwater and marine species known only from a few specimens collected from Madagascar and the island of Réunion.
Dorothea's wriggler (Allomicrodesmus dorotheae) is a reef-dwelling fish known only from two specimens, one collected from the Great Barrier Reef and the other from the Marshall Islands.

Bentley's mormyrid (Marcusenius bentleyi), Wagenia Falls whiptailed catfish (Phractura fasciata), Wagenia Rapids loach catfish (Dolichamphilius longiceps), and Wagenia Falls claroteid catfish (Amarginops platus) are all known only from Wagenia Falls, the last in the Stanley Falls cataract system.
The Chindwin torrent catfish (Amblyceps tuberculatum) is confined to fast-flowing hillstreams of the Chindwin River drainage.
The narrow-barred butterflyfish (Amphichaetodon melbae) is known only from a few specimens collected from the San Felix Islands off the coast of Chile and Easter Island.
Lampe's mountain catfish (Amphilius lampei) is known only from a single, undefined locality within the Shabelle River drainage of central Ethiopia.
The Mai-Ndombe mountain catfish (Amphilius opisthophthalmus) is known only from a few specimens collected from Lake Mai-Ndombe.
The Allcuquiro killifish (Anablepsoides monticola) is known only from a single montane forest brook in south-central Ecuador (Morona Santiago province).
The longfin Pacific anchovy (Anchoa analis) is a small, silvery fish confined to the coastal waters of northwestern Mexico.
The Chame Point anchovy (Anchoa chamensis) is known only from the Gulf of Panama.
Jelski's bristlenose catfish (Ancistrus jelskii) is known only from a small area of south-central Peru (Junín department).
The Astola combtooth blenny (Antennablennius velifer) is known only from tidal areas on Astola Island.
The Gulf of Guinea seaperch (Anthias cyprinoides) is known only from a few specimens collected during the 1980s off Annobón Island in the Gulf of Guinea.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The Saint Helena seaperch (Anthias helenensis) is known only from eight specimens collected from the Saint Helena Seamount Chain.
The Spanish toothcarp (Aphanius iberus) is confined to coastal Spain and Algeria.
Wischmann's longfin (Aphyolebias wischmanni) is a type of killifish known only from a backwater of the Chipiria and Amaquiria rivers, in the Ucayali drainage of central Peru.
Rass' blind cusk-eel (Aphyonus rassi) is known only from two specimens collected north of the Cape Verde Islands, and another from the eastern Caribbean Sea.
Heinemann's killifish (Aphyosemion heinemanni) is confined to tributaries (forest brooks) of the Nyong River.
Wuendsch's killifish (Aphyosemion wuendschi) is confined to a single, swampy rainforest creek of the Ngounie River, in the central Chaillu Mountains of Gabon.
Nijssen's dwarf cichlid (Apistogramma nijsseni) is known only from the Quebrada Carahuayte, a small blackwater stream in the Copal River drainage.
The Nanay dwarf cichlid (Apistogramma pantalone) is known only from the upper Nanay River.
species.iucn: Apistogramma pantalone Romer, Romer, Soares & Hahn, 2006

species.e: The Madre de Dios dwarf cichlid (Apistogramma rubrolineata) is known only from three localities within the Madre de Dios drainage, two of which are in protected areas.
The gracile finless eel (Apterichtus gracilis) is known only from a few specimens collected off the coast of Sierra Leone and Guinea.
The Jurubidá knifefish (Apteronotus jurubidae) is known only from the Jurubidá River.
The South China deep-sea hatchet-fish (Araiophos eastropas) is known only from the South China Sea.
The Madagascar kob (Argyrosomus hololepidotus) is confined to estuaries and mangroves on the southeastern coast of Madagagascar, where it is threatened by overfishing.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The silver conger eel (Ariosoma mellissii) is known only from a few specimens collected from the waters around Saint Helena.
Cantor's pufferfish (Arothron carduus) is known only from two specimens collected from disjunct coral reef localities off the Malay Peninsula and in the Ryukyu Islands.
The emaciated worm-eel (Asarcenchelys longimanus) is known only from two specimens collected off the northeastern coast of Brazil.
Herald's reef sole (Aseraggodes heraldi) is known only from two specimens collected from Kwajalein Atoll in the Marshall Islands.
Herre's reef sole (Aseraggodes herrei) is known only from a few specimens collected off the Revillagigedos Islands, Galápagos Islands, Cocos Island, and the tip of the Baja California Peninsula.
Holcom's reef sole (Aseraggodes holcomi) is known only from a small number of specimens collected in shallow waters off northern Oahu.
The New Caledonia reef sole (Aseraggodes magnoculus) is known only from three specimens collected from two localities off the southwestern coast of Grande Terre, New Caledonia.
Ramsa's reef sole (Aseraggodes ramsaii) is known only from a few specimens collected off Lord Howe Island and southern New Caledonia.
The Ukhrul danio (Aspidoparia ukhrulensis) is known only from two localities within the Ukhrul River.
The Cáchira naked suckermouth catfish (Astroblepus cacharas) is known only from a small tributary of the Cáchira River.
Martinez's naked suckermouth catfish (Astroblepus martinezi) is known only from a small tributary of the Tay River, in the upper Sinú River drainage.
Whymper's naked suckermouth catfish (Astroblepus whymperi) is confined to fast-flowing Andean streams within the Esmeraldas River drainage.
Bean's silverside (Atherinella beani) is known only from a few specimens collected from estuaries in coastal Nicaragua and Panama.
The broadstripe silverside (Atherinella nesiotes) is known only from a few specimens collected from the waters off the Galápagos Islands.
Chabanaud's upside-down catfish (Atopochilus chabanaudi) is known only from an area of Stanley Pool near Brazzaville.
The black-spot croaker (Atrobucca kyushini) is known only from the northwestern coast of Borneo.
The estuary catfish (Ayarnangra estuarius) is known only from a few specimens collected from the tidal reaches of the lower Irrawaddy River.
The Chittagong perch (Badis chittagongis) is known only from a few hillstreams in southeastern Bangladesh.
The Siamese perch (Badis siamensis) is confined to peninsular Thailand and the island of Phuket, where it is threatened by loss of habitat and overcollection for the international aquarium trade.
The Chaptis bahaba (Bahaba chaptis) is confined to the coastal waters of the Bay of Bengal, where it is taken as bycatch.
Sinkler's bangana (Bangana sinkleri) is known only from the upper Taeng River.
Parfait's blind cusk-eel (Barathronus parfaiti) is known only from two disjunct deepwater localities in the north-central and northeastern Atlantic.
The elongated searsid (Barbantus elongatus) is a type of smelt confined to the deep waters of the South Atlantic Ridge.
The saddle-banded goby (Barbulifer mexicanus) is a near-shore species known only from the tip of the Baja California Peninsula, the Tres Marías Islands, and central coastal Mexico.
The Bonar baril (Barilius bonarensis) is a type of cyprinid fish known only from its original description in 1912 from northwestern India (Uttarakhand).
Evezard's baril (Barilius evezardi) is known only from a few historical records over a wide area of southern India.
The unexpected snake-eel (Bascanichthys inopinatus) is known only from three specimens collected from two localities off Puerto Rico in the 1960s and 70s.
The Nepalese naked catfish (Batasio macronotus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Ganges River drainage in eastern Nepal.
The Irrawaddy naked catfish (Batasio procerus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the upper Irrawaddy River drainage in northern Myanmar.
The Cagayan grenadier (Bathygadus sulcatus) is a large deep-sea fish known only from deep waters off Cagayan Island.
The twin-spotted frillfin goby (Bathygobius geminatus) is known only from two shallow water localities in the western Atlantic (eastern Florida and northern Puerto Rico).
Nielsen's slickhead (Bathylaco nielseni) is a type of deep-sea smelt known only from two localities in the eastern central Atlantic and western Indian Ocean.
Derjugin's ronquil (Bathymaster derjugini) is confined to a small area off southeastern Russia and the Kuril Islands, where it is threatened by coastal development and pollution.
The Tasman Sea spiderfish (Bathypterois oddi) is a deep-sea species known only from a few specimens collected off the southern coast of New Zealand.
Brien's loach catfish (Belonoglanis brieni) is known only from a single channel within Stanley Pool.

The Mekong betta (Betta stiktos) is known only from a small area of the Srepok River in northeastern Cambodia, but is expected to occur as well in the lower Kong River in southern Laos and northeastern Cambodia.
The few-rayed pipefish (Bhanotia pauciradiata) is a poorly-known coastal pipefish known only from a single       specimen collected from a rocky coral reef slope at Maumere, Flores, in 1995.
The New Caledonian silverside (Bleheratherina pierucciae) is known only from a dozen specimens collected from two rivers in southern Grande Terre, and from a third locality in the north.
The five-striped hogfish (Bodianus paraleucosticticus) is known only from a few specimens collected off Rarotonga and Papua New Guinea, and from a photo taken off New Caledonia.
The sunburnt hogfish (Bodianus solatus) is confined to a small area off Western Australia.
The Kyushu-Palau Ridge hogfish (Bodianus thoracotaeniatus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Kyushu-Palau Ridge, east of Okinawa.
The striped boga (Boops lineatus) is confined to coastal areas of the eastern Arabian Peninsula.
The Guinean flounder (Bothus guibei) is known only from a few specimens collected from shallow waters off the islands of Annobón and São Tomé.
The emperor loach (Botia udomritthiruji) is confined to hillstreams within the upper Great Tenasserim River drainage.
The bumblebee fish (Brachygobius xanthozonus) is known only from a few specimens collected in coastal Borneo and Java.
Abel's robber tetra (Brycinus abeli) is known only from Fort Sibut on the Oubangui River.
Medem's tetra (Brycon medemi) is known only from a few localities in the upper Atrato River drainage.
The Guiza characin (Bryconamericus guizae) is known only from tributary streams of the Guiza River.
The Ichó characin (Bryconamericus ichoensis) is known only from a single tributary of the Ichó River.
The Sucio characin (Bryconamericus multiradiatus) is known only from a few specimens collected from two localities within the Sucio River drainage.
Bruce's pugheaded pipefish (Bulbonaricus brucei) is known only from a few specimens collected from coral reefs off the coast of Tanzania.
The Icelandic viviparous brotula (Bythites islandicus) is known only from a handful of specimens collected off the southeastern coast of Iceland.
The bigeye callibus (Cabillus macrophthalmus) is a type of marine goby known only from a few specimens collected in the Flores Sea.
The ridgefin eel (Callechelys springeri) is known only from four specimens collected in the 1940s and 1960s from off the southeastern coast of the United States.

species.v: South China Sea The Macclesfield dragonet
species.e: The Macclesfield Bank is an elongated sunken atoll of underwater reefs and shoals located in the central South China Sea The Macclesfield dragonet (Callionymus macclesfieldensis) is confined to the deeper waters of the Macclesfield Bank.

Both are threatened by fisheries bycatch and collection for use in “traditional medicine.” Whitehead's deepwater dragonet (Callionymus whiteheadi) is known only from three specimens collected off Java, Bali and the Kangean Islands.
The dwarf pipefish (Campichthys nanus) is known only from a few specimens collected during the 1970s from coastal northern Mozambique.
The donkey-faced mormyrid (Campylomormyrus cassaicus) is known only from two specimens collected from the Luachimo River and another from the Kasai River main channel.
The Luapula mormyrid (Campylomormyrus luapulaensis) is known only from two localities within the Luapula River.
The long-tailed filefish (Cantherhines longicaudus) is known only from a few specimens collected across a wide area of the tropical Indo-Pacific.
The Nuku Hiva filefish (Cantherhines nukuhiva) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Marquesas Islands and the Tuamotu Archipelago.
The Andaman sharpnose pufferfish (Canthigaster investigatoris) is known only from two specimens collected in 1910 off of the Andaman Islands.
The Mascarene sharpnose pufferfish (Canthigaster punctata) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Mascarene Plateau.
Meder's snailfish (Careproctus mederi) is endemic to the Sea of Okhotsk, where it appears to be rare.
The Burwood Bank snailfish (Careproctus minimus) is known only from two specimens collected from the Burdwood Bank.
The Bahamian false moray eel (Catesbya pseudomuraena) is known only from a few specimens collected at two shallow reef localities in the Bahamas.
The yellowbar tilefish (Caulolatilus williamsi) is known only from four specimens collected from the Bahamas and Saint Croix in the Virgin Islands.
The many-spined worm-goby (Cerdale prolata) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Gulf of Panama.
Hempel's whalefish (Cetomimus hempeli) is known only from a handful of specimens collected from deep waters surrounding the Canary Islands and Madeira.
The Cortez pike-blenny (Chaenopsis coheni) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Gulf of California and Ángel de la Guarda Island.
The delta pike-blenny (Chaenopsis deltarrhis) is known only from a few specimens collected over a relatively wide area of coastal Central America as well as Cocos Island.

The Medellín bristlemouth catfish (Chaetostoma aburrensis) is known only from a now-lost type specimen collected from an inprecise locality within the Cauca River drainage during the early twentieth century.
The Arakan snakehead (Channa pulchra) is a type of fish confined to streams in the Arakan Mountains of south-central Myanmar.
The Ogooué eel catfish (Channallabes ogooensis) is known only from specimens collected in the Franceville area of Gabon.
The Tocantins darter (Characidium stigmosum) is possibly confined to a few tributaries of the upper Tocantins River in Goiás state.
Kazuko's false moray eel (Chlopsis kazuko) is known only from five specimens collected from the Gulf of California, Malpelo Island, and off the coast of Costa Rica.
The girdled fairy-wrasse (Cirrhilabrus balteatus) is known only from the Marshall Islands.
The dusky fairy-wrasse (Cirrhilabrus brunneus) is known only from a few specimens collected off Borneo, Sulawesi and Cebu in the Philippines.
The whip-fin fairy-wrasse (Cirrhilabrus filamentosus) is a reef-dweller known only from the Java Sea, where it is threatened by collection for the international aquarium trade and by cyanide fishing.
The diamond-tail fairy-wrasse (Cirrhilabrus rhomboidalis) is largely confined to the Caroline and Marshall Islands, with vagrants occasionally recorded from Palau and Saipan in the Mariana Islands.

The rosy-scaled fairy-wrasse (Cirrhilabrus rubrisquamis) is known only from the waters around Sri Lanka, the Maldives and the Chagos Archipelago, where it is threatened by degradation of their its coral reef habitat and collection for the international aquarium trade.
The Tenasserim mud carp (Cirrhinus rubirostris) is known only from the Great Tenasserim River, where it is potentially threatened by dam development.

The white-spotted hawkfish (Cirrhitus albopunctatus) is known only from two specimens collected in shallow waters off Niuafo'ou Island in Tonga and an additional observation record off Tutuila in American Samoa.
The big-chinned sandab (Citharichthys gnathus) is a type of flatfish known only from a few specimens collected from a single deepwater locality off the Galápagos Islands.
The Lake Victoria snake catfish (Clariallabes petricola) is known only from the northern part of Lake Victoria and from an area of the Victoria Nile near Owen Falls.
The African Creole wrasse (Clepticus africanus) is known only from the coastal waters of São Tomé in the Gulf of Guinea.
Lin's spined loach (Cobitis arenae) is known only from the Xi and Dong rivers, tributaries of the Pearl River in southern China.
The Mu spined loach (Cobitis guttata) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Mu River.
The flat catfish (Cochlefelis insidiator) is known only from four specimens collected in the Fly River delta of Papua New Guinea and from coastal northern Australia, west of Darwin.
The Japanese worm-eel (Coloconger japonicus) is known only from deep waters of the East China Sea.
The smooth-belly pellonuline (Congothrissa gossei) is a type of herring known only from a few specimens collected from two localities within the middle Congo River drainage.
The Pilbara eel blenny (Congrogadus winterbottomi) is known only from Middle Mangrove Island and Exmouth Gulf, off Western Australia.
The blackbar coris (Coris nigrotaenia) is a type of wrasse known only from the waters of coastal Oman and Masirah Island.
Reynolds' corydoras catfish (Corydoras reynoldsi) is known only from a tributary of the Orteguasa River.
The Palawan grenadier (Coryphaenoides camurus) is known only from a few specimens collected in 1909 from deep waters off Palawan, in the western Sulu Sea.
Herald's pipefish (Cosmocampus heraldi) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Juan Fernández and Desventuradas islands off Chile.

The deepwater pipefish (Cosmocampus profundus) is known only from a few specimens collected over a wide area of the western Atlantic, including off the southeastern United States, the Virgin Islands, the Yucatán Peninsula, and possibly Curaçao.
The Española blenny (Cottoclinus canops) is known only from two specimens collected from a tidal pool on Española during the late twentieth century.
Guichenot's goby (Cotylopus acutipinnis) is a freshwater and marine species confined to Mauritius and Reunion.
The Pima hardyhead (Craterocephalus pimatuae) is known only from the junction of the Pima and Tua rivers, tributaries of the Purari River.
Yanatil's characin (Creagrutus yanatili) is known only from the Urubamba / Vilcanota River and its tributary, the Yanatili River.
The Karanteen seabream (Crenidens macracanthus) is known only from two specimens collected during the nineteenth century off Pakistan and India.
The Gulf of Thailand shrimp-goby (Cryptocentrus leonis) is confined to marine and brackish waters along the Gulf of Thailand.
The hidden blenny (Cryptotrema seftoni) is known only from a deep rocky reef off the northern end of Guardian Angel Island, in the northern Gulf of California, where it was last collected in 1952.
The La Miel killifish (Cynodonichthys boehlkei) is known only from temporary streams and pools within the La Miel River drainage.
The hake weakfish (Cynoscion nortoni) is known only from six specimens collected from the coasts of western Ecuador and northwestern Peru.
The Kien Giang carp (Cyprinus melanes) is confined to the Kien Giang River.
The sand stargazer (Dactylagnus peratikos) is known only from two localities on the coast of Costa Rica and Panama.
Gerring's toadfish (Daector gerringi) is a freshwater and marine species confined to the lower reaches of the San Juan and Baudó rivers of western Colombia (Chocó department).
The West African snake-eel (Dalophis obtusirostris) is known only from two specimens collected from estuaries in Senegal and Mauritania in 1972.
The largescale wrasse (Decodon grandisquamis) is known only from coastal southern Mozambique.
Fourmanoir's sea bream (Dentex fourmanoiri) is known only from a few specimens collected from the waters surrounding Grande Terre and the Chesterfield Islands, New Caledonia.
The whiskereye clingfish (Derilissus kremnobates) is known only from Arrowsmith Bank.

The tailspot clingfish (Derilissus lombardii) is known only from two specimens, the first collected from a deep coral wall off Lee Stocking Island in the Bahamas, and a second photographed off Grand Cayman.
The dwarf clingfish (Derilissus nanus) is known only from a few deepwater localities in the Bahama Banks, including the Plana Cays, Great Inagua, and Acklins Island.
The gold-striped danio (Devario chrysotaeniatus) is confined to tributaries and smaller streams within the upper Mekong drainage.
The Bolaven danio (Devario salmonatus) is confined to the Bolaven Plateau of southeastern Laos, within the Kong River drainage.

Bentley's mormyrid (Marcusenius bentleyi), Wagenia Falls whiptailed catfish (Phractura fasciata), Wagenia Rapids loach catfish (Dolichamphilius longiceps), and Wagenia Falls claroteid catfish (Amarginops platus) are all known only from Wagenia Falls, the last in the Stanley Falls cataract system.
Bleeker's pipefish (Doryichthys heterosoma) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Sambas and Lupar rivers of western Borneo and from the Natuna Islands.
The Arabian Sea flagtail pipefish (Doryrhamphus aurolineatus) is known only from two specimens collected off Masirah Island, Oman.
The glowtail pipefish (Dunckerocampus chapmani) is known only from shallow lagoons in a small area of southwestern Grande Terre, New Caledonia.
The Japanese blobfish (Ebinania brephocephala) is a little-known species confined to the southern coast of Japan.
The slit-pore tube blenny (Ekemblemaria lira) is known only from three specimens collected in the early 1960s from coastal northern Ecuador.
The Hawaiian spinecheek sleeper goby (Eleotris sandwicensis) is confined to lowland streams of the larger Hawaiian Islands.
The elusive signal blenny (Emblemaria walkeri) is known only from a few specimens collected in the western and central-eastern Gulf of California.
The Vanuatu lefteye flounder (Engyprosopon vanuatuensis) is known only from a small number of specimens collected off Vanuatu.
The Sala y Gómez sandfish (Enigmapercis acutirostris) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Sala y Gomez Ridge.
Shen's triplefin blenny (Enneapterygius sheni) is known only from the southern tip of Taiwan, though it may perhaps range farther south to offshore islands.
Deguide's barb (Enteromius deguidei) is known only from marshes along the Boteli River, a tributary of the Tshuapa River.
The Kasuku barb (Enteromius papilio) is known only from an unnamed tributary of the Kasuku River.
The Tana barb (Enteromius pleurogramma) is known only from a few specimens collected within the Blue Nile basin, including Lake Tana.
The pygmy barb (Enteromius pygmaeus) is known only from a single rainforest stream within the middle Congo River drainage.
The Kavalli barb (Enteromius tetraspilus) is known only from the Kavalli and upper Ituri rivers.
The Somali grouper (Epinephelus indistinctus) is known only from the coastal waters of Oman and northern Somalia.
The plumb grouper (Epinephelus trophis) is known only from two specimens collected in 1974 from Dillon Shoals.
The Samar Sea ponyfish (Equulites laterofenestra) is known only from shallow tidal waters and estuaries near Leyte.
The Schutunga catfish (Erethistoides sicula) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Schutunga River, a tributary of the Mansai River.
The Pacific menhaden (Ethmidium maculatum) is a type of small pelagic fish confined to the continental shelf of Peru and northern Chile, where it is subject to intense fishing pressure.
The Pacific sand flounder (Etropus pacificus) is known only from two specimens collected off Panama and northern Chile.
The blue-spotted leatherjacket (Eubalichthys caeruleoguttatus) is a type of filefish known only from a few specimens collected in the coastal waters of northwestern Australia.
The Hawaiian barbeled dragonfish (Eustomias dinema) is known only from a few specimens collected in the waters of the Hawaiian Islands.
The Cape Verde barbeled dragonfish (Eustomias insularum) is known only from deep waters of the Cape Verde Rise.
The Gulf of Guinea barbeled dragonfish (Eustomias monoclonoides) is a deepwater species known only from a small area of the Gulf of Guinea.
The spreading barbeled dragonfish (Eustomias patulus) is known only from two records (off Puerto Rico and between the Canary and Cape Verde Islands).
The enigmatic goby (Evermannia longipinnis) is known only from a single imprecise locality thought to be in the northwestern Gulf of California.
The bicoloured sponge goby (Evermannichthys bicolor) is known only from five specimens collected off Jamaica, Navassa and western Haiti.
The tenant sponge goby (Evermannichthys convictor) is known only from two disjunct localities (Green Cay, Bahamas and coastal northern Jamaica).
Herre's dwarf goby (Eviota herrei) is known only from the Samoan Islands.
The Peruvian flying fish (Exocoetus peruvianus) is confined to a small area of the northwestern South American continental shelf from Ecuador to southern Peru.
The Coroico armoured catfish (Farlowella altocorpus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Beni River drainage.
The slender armoured catfish (Farlowella gracilis) is known only from a few localities in southwestern Colombia (Caquetá department).
Dawson's pipefish (Festucalex prolixus) is known only from six specimens collected in 1929 from two disjunct localities (southern Philippines and off the coast of northwestern New Guinea).
The Madagascar cardinalfish (Foa madagascariensis) is known only from two specimens, now lost, collected off the coast of southwestern Madagascar in the early 1930s.
The Ecucu killifish (Fundulopanchax avichang) is known only from small temporary pools within the Ecucu River drainage.
The Mamfue killifish (Fundulopanchax intermittens) is known only from two localities within the Mamfue River.
The Philippine rattail (Gadomus magnifilis) is a deep-sea species known only from a few specimens collected during the early twentieth century from three localities in the Philippines.

The Domingo mosquito fish (Gambusia dominicensis) is naturally confined to two lakes on Hispaniola (Lake Azuei in southeastern Haiti (Ouest department), and Lake Enriquillo in the southwestern Dominican Republic (Independencia province).
The Tam Duong garra (Garra bibarbatus) is confined to the Tam Duong River.
Kottelat's garra (Garra cyrano) is known from the Leuk, Theun and Kong tributaries in Laos, where it is restricted to the upper parts of the respective drainages in areas with strong current.
The Tubarão driftwood catfish (Glanidium catharinensis) is confined to the Tubarão River.
The line-cheek goby (Glossogobius sparsipapillus) is known only from the tidal zone of the Mekong delta and from the lower parts of the Mekong River in southern Vietnam and southern Cambodia.
The short-finned mountain catfish (Glyptothorax brevipinnis) is known only from four specimens collected in 1923 from an undefined locality in India.
The Urutty mountain catfish (Glyptothorax malabarensis) is known only from a single hillstream within the Valapattanam River drainage.
The Great Meteor conger eel (Gnathophis codoniphorus) is known only from the Great Meteor Seamount.
The Tsinan gudgeon (Gnathopogon tsinanensis) is confined to a small area of northeastern China (Shangdong).
Graham's goby (Gobioides grahamae) is known only from a few specimens collected in muddy areas along the northern South American coast (Guyana to northern Brazil).
The dwarf freshwater goby (Gobiopterus stellatus) is a little-known species confined to Luzon.
Schmidt's goby (Gobius strictus) is known only from a small number of specimens collected across the Mediterreanean, which may or may not have been misidentified.
The fin-joined goby (Gobulus birdsongi) is known only from two mangrove streams flowing into the Panama Canal, where it is threatened by loss of habitat.
The Mananara du Nord catfish (Gogo atratus) is confined to the Mananara du Nord River.
Whitehead's gizzard shad (Gonialosa whiteheadi) is known only from two specimens collected from an estuary in southern Myanmar.
The Pacific horsehair eel (Gordiichthys combibus) is known only from a few specimens collected in shallow waters off northwestern Colombia, but may be more wide ranging.
The irksone snake-eel (Gordiichthys ergodes) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Gulf of Mexico.
The golden basslet (Gramma dejongi) is known only from a few specimens collected from coral reefs off southwestern Cuba and Little Cayman Island.
Ginsburg's sleeper goby (Guavina micropus) is confined to freshwater streams and brackish waters on the Pacific coast of Costa Rica and Panama.
The Eilat cardinalfish (Gymnapogon melanogaster) is known only from two specimens collected in the Gulf of Aqaba.
The oblong large-eye bream (Gymnocranius oblongus) is known only from six specimens discovered in a fish market in New Caledonia.
Chu's naked carp (Gymnocypris chui) is known only from four endorheic mountain lakes in southern and western Tibet.
Bacallado's moray eel (Gymnothorax bacalladoi) is known only from three specimens collected from the Canary Islands and Madeira.
The wide-mouth moray eel (Gymnothorax eurygnathos) is known only from two specimens collected from the Gulf of California and off El Salvador.
The sawtooth moray eel (Gymnothorax serratidens) is known only from a few specimens collected from coastal southwestern Colombia and northwestern Peru.
Pelicier's wrasse (Halichoeres pelicieri) is confined to deepwater reef slopes off Mauritius.
Raisner's wrasse (Halichoeres raisneri) is known only from relatively deep waters off the Galápagos Islands.
The sign wrasse (Halichoeres signifer) is confined to shallow waters off the coast of Oman.
The Galápagos batfish (Halieutopsis tumifrons) is a type of anglerfish known only from two specimens collected from deep waters within the Galápagos Islands.

Tweddle's cichlid (Haplochromis tweddlei) is known only from lakes Chiuta and Chilwa and associated rivers in southeastern Malawi and northern Mozambique, where it is threatened by overfishing and drought.
The uncombed blenny (Haptoclinus apectolophus) is known only from Arrowsmith Bank.
The Solor triplefin blenny (Helcogramma solorensis) is known only from three specimens collected on Solor Island in the Lesser Sunda Islands.
The Antarctic triplefin blenny (Helcogrammoides antarcticus) is a subtidal species known only from a few specimens collected from Paradise Bay, on the Antarctic Peninsula.
Opic's eel (Hemerorhinus opici) is known only from three specimens collected from the coastal waters of Ghana, Senegal and Republic of Congo.
The Quang Binh catfish (Hemibagrus centralus) is known only from hillstreams within the Annamite Mountains of central Vietnam (Quang Binh province).
The Lai Chau catfish (Hemibagrus songdaensis) is known only from the upper Black River in northwestern Vietnam (Lai Chau province).
The Risaralda characin (Hemibrycon cairoense) is known only from Los Ramirez and Italica creeks, small tributaries of the Risaralda River.
The Santa Marta characin (Hemibrycon santamartae) is known only from two disjunct localities within the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia (La Guajira and Magdalena departments).
species.iucn: Hemibrycon santamartae Román-Valencia, Ruiz-C., García-Alzate & Taphorn, 2010

species.e: The Santander characin (Hemibrycon virolinica) is known only from a few creeks and rivers in northern Colombia (Santander department).
The Ky Cung sharpbelly (Hemiculter elongatus) is confined to the Ky Cung River.
Krempf's sharpbelly (Hemiculter krempfi) is known only from the Cai and Da Rang rivers of central Vietnam (Khanh Hoa and Phu Yen provinces).
Tchang's sharpbelly (Hemiculter tchangi) is known only from the upper reaches of the Yangtze River in central Chinga (Sichuan).
The Red Sea thicklip wrasse (Hemigymnus sexfasciatus) is known only from a couple of records originating in the Red Sea.
The Nujiang river loach (Hemimyzon nujiangensis) is confined to the upper Salween River in Yunnan.
The white-ring garden eel (Heteroconger canabus) is known only from sandy slopes near reefs in the southwestern Gulf of California.
The Portuguese footballfish (Himantolophus compressus) is a type of deep-sea anglerfish is known only from a single, now-lost specimen collected off the coast of Portugal.
The bullneck seahorse (Hippocampus minotaur) is known only from a few specimens collected from southeastern Australia.
The Ascension seaperch (Holanthias caudalis) is known only from two specimens collected during the 1970s from the waters around Ascenscion Island.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: Günther's seaperch (Holanthias fronticinctus) is confined to deep reefs off Saint Helena.
The Red Sea roughy (Hoplostethus marisrubri) is known only from five specimens collected from a single locality (possibly a seamount) in the middle of the Red Sea.
The metallic roughy (Hoplostethus metallicus) is a deep-sea species known only from a small number of specimens collected throughout the central Philippines.
The Amaron tetra (Hyphessobrycon amaronensis) is known only from a few creeks and rivers within a small area of southern Colombia (Putumayo department).
The Acandí tetra (Hyphessobrycon columbianus) was, until relatively recently, known only from a few specimens collected from the Acandí River drainage.
Sebastian's tetra (Hyphessobrycon sebastiani) is known only from two disjunct localities within the Calima and San Juan rivers of western coastal Colombia (Chocó and Valle del Cauca departments).
The bicoloured hamlet (Hypoplectrus maculiferus) is known only from reefs off Havana, Cuba and Saint Barthélemy, but presumably ranges more widely.
The Huong barb (Hypsibarbus annamensis) is known only from specimens collected from the Huong River in 1936.
The chain lampeye (Hypsopanchax catenatus) is known only from a single rainforest brook within the Ogooué River drainage in southeastern Gabon.
The Ascension sand-eel (Ichthyapus insularis) is confined to the shoreline of Ascension Island.
Meek's catfish (Ictalurus australis) is confined to the Blanco and Pánuco rivers of eastern Mexico, where it is threatened mainly by overfishing.
The Lerma catfish (Ictalurus dugesii) is confined to the Turbio and Ayuquila rivers.
The La Quebradona three-barbeled catfish (Imparfinis timana) is known only from La Quebradona creek, a small tributary of the Guarapas River.
species.iucn: Imparfinis timana Ortega-Lara, Milani, DoNascimiento, Villa-Navarro & Maldonado-Ocampo, 2011

species.e: Valenciennes' razorfish (Iniistius cyanifrons) is known only from coastal southern India off Pondicherry and Madras.
The sixband hawkfish (Isocirrhitus sexfasciatus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the shallow waters around the Marshall Islands, the Tuamotu Archipelago and Rapa, French Polynesia.
The Venezuelan herring (Jenkinsia parvula) is known only from a few specimens collected off the coast of Venezuela.
The smooth croaker (Johnius laevis) is confined to the coastal waters of northern Australia and southern New Guinea, where it is frequently taken as prawn fishery bycatch.
The Sierra Leone sleeper goby (Kribia leonensis) is known only from three localities in eastern Sierra Leone.
The Salele flagtail (Kuhlia salelea) is a type of freshwater fish confined to a few Samoan rivers.
The Lake Malawi yellowfish (Labeobarbus latirostris) is an uncommon species endemic to Lake Malawi, from where it ascends the Bua and Shire rivers to spawn.
The spotcheek blenny (Labrisomus pomaspilus) is known only from a few tide pool localities in coastal southwestern Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.
The Baja blenny (Labrisomus wigginsi) is confined to the Pacific coast of the central and southern Baja California Peninsula.
The Izmir minnow (Ladigesocypris mermere) is known only from a few specimens collected from southwestern Anatolia.
Symoens' cichlid (Lamprologus symoensi) is known only from two effluents of the Lufira River.

The bristly fish (Laocypris hispida) is known only from the Nam Leuk and Nam San (a small tributary of the Negum Reservoir) in northern Laos, where it is threatened by overfishing and loss of habitat.
The Guinea wrasse (Lappanella guineensis) is known only from relatively deep rocky reefs off the coast of Senegal and Guinea in West Africa.
The four-line wrasse (Larabicus quadrilineatus) is confined to the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
The Nariño lebiasina (Lebiasina narinensis) is known only from a single ravine in southwestern Colombia (Nariño department).

The Solomons freshwater goby (Lentipes solomonensis) is an amphidromous species known only from a handful of specimens collected from three streams on three different islands within the Solomons (Ranogga, Rendova and Makira).
Fowler's sea robin (Lepidotrigla venusta) is a type of bottom-feeding fish known only from the waters off the eastern coast of Luzon.
Hose's barb (Leptobarbus hosii) is confined to a few rivers in northern Borneo (Sarawak and Sabah, Malaysia).
The slender barracundina (Lestidiops gracilis) is a deep-sea fish confined to the eastern coast of New Zealand.
The Atlantic false brotula (Leucobrotula adipata) is known only from seven specimens collected off the coast of western Europe.
The Ky-Phu loach (Liniparhomaloptera monoloba) is known only from Ky-Phu creek in northern Vietnam.
The minute clingfish (Liobranchia stria) is known only from specimens collected off Guam and Saipan.
The Persian mullet (Liza persicus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the shallow coastal waters of Qatar and Bahrain.
Myers' dottyback (Lubbockichthys myersi) is known only from a single museum specimen collected in the waters off Guam, along with a few observations.
Lortet's barbel (Luciobarbus lorteti) is confined to the lower Orontes River in Syria and Turkey.
The Gulf of Guinea snapper (Lutjanus endecacanthus) is known only from a few specimens collected during the nineteenth century.
Sola's goby (Lythrypnus solanensis) is confined to the coastal waters of Gorgona Island, off the coast of Colombia.
The Hpa Lap spiny eel (Macrognathus obscurus) is known only from specimens collected from a single stream in northern Myanmar.
The black paradise fish (Macropodus spechti) is a type of gourami known only from the Thu Bon and Houng river drainages of central Vietnam.
The Costa Rican blenny (Malacoctenus costaricanus) is known only from a few historical records from the western coasts of Costa Rica and El Salvador.
The reticulated wrasse (Malapterus reticulatus) is known only from shallow waters off the Juan Fernández and Desventuradas Islands.

Bentley's mormyrid (Marcusenius bentleyi), Wagenia Falls whiptailed catfish (Phractura fasciata), Wagenia Rapids loach catfish (Dolichamphilius longiceps), and Wagenia Falls claroteid catfish (Amarginops platus) are all known only from Wagenia Falls, the last in the Stanley Falls cataract system.
The orange pipefish (Maroubra yasudai) is known only from the Izu Oceanic Park off the southeastern coast of Honshu, Japan.
Boulenger's cichlid (Mchenga inornata) is known only from two specimens collected during the early twentieth century from an unknown locality within Lake Malawi.
Carpenter's yellowtop jewelfish (Meganthias carpenteri) is known only from two specimens obtained from a fish market in Nigeria.
The Tonlé San carp (Mekongina bibarba) is confined to the Tonlé San River.
Ebeling's bigscale (Melamphaes ebelingi) is a type of deep-sea fish known only from a few specimens collected throughout the tropical Atlantic.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: Hubbs' bigscale (Melamphaes hubbsi) is known only from deep waters near Saint Helena.
The Plateada silverside (Membras argentea) is known only from three specimens collected during the 1940s from a single locality off northern Colombia.
The Cortez hake (Merluccius hernandezi) is a cod-like fish endemic to the deeper waters of the Gulf of California.
Nichols' climbing gourami (Microctenopoma lineatum) is known only from a few localities in the Central African Republic and northern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Miller's climbing gourami (Microctenopoma milleri) is known only from lower Congo and its tributary, the Lunyonzo River.
The Congo worm-goby (Microdesmus africanus) is known only from two specimens collected from the Congo River estuary.
The blind worm-goby (Microdesmus luscus) is known only from a few specimens collected from three, widely-separated, shallow coral reefs (Dominica, Puerto Rico and Panama).
The short-bodied pipefish (Micrognathus brevicorpus) is known only from coral reefs surrounding Grande Terre, New Caledonia.
Sanzo's deepwater cardinalfish (Microichthys sanzoi) is known only from the southeastern coast of Sicily.

The slender pipefish (Microphis caudocarinatus) is known only from two specimens, the first collected from the Tawarin River of northwestern New Guinea in 1903, and the other from Sumbawa in the Lesser Sunda Islands in 1995.
The Dumbéa River pipefish (Microphis cruentus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Dumbéa River.
The spinach pipefish (Microphis spinachioides) is known only from the Sepik, May and Ramu rivers of Papua New Guinea, where it may be threatened by habitat degradation.
The Arica croaker (Micropogonias fasciatus) is known only from two specimens collected off the northern coast of Chile in 1962.
The Kyé upside-down catfish (Microsynodontis nannoculus) is known only from the Kyé River.
Dawson's pipefish (Minyichthys inusitatus) is known only from as single juvenile collected in relatively deep waters off the coast of Panama.
Rendahl's weather loach (Misgurnus multimaculatus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the 1940s from central coastal Vietnam (Hué province).
The western crested pipefish (Mitotichthys meraculus) is confined to seagrass meadows in the vicinity of Flinders Bay and Perth, Western Australia.
Taning's one-jawed eel (Monognathus taningi) is known only from two specimens collected during the 1930s from deep waters of the Cape Verde Rise.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The Saint Helena deepwater flounder (Monolene helenensis) is known only from few specimens collected north of Saint Helena.
Hodgart's swamp eel (Monopterus hodgarti) is known only from its original description during the early twentieth century from northeatern India (Arunachal Pradesh).
The small mormyrid (Mormyrops parvus) is confined to the lower Congo River.
The Margarita mullet (Mugil margaritae) is known only from a small number of specimens collected from two, widely-spaced localities off the coast of Venezuela.
species.iucn: Mugil margaritae Menezes, Nirchio, Olivera & Siccharamirez, 2015

species.e: The Okhotsk sculpin (Myoxocephalus tuberculatus) is known only from the Sea of Okhotsk, where it is potentially threatened by overfishing and pollution.
The Taiwanese soldierfish (Myripristis formosa) is known only from four collections off Taiwan.
The Tiki soldierfish (Myripristis tiki) is known only from a few specimens collected from Rapa in French Polynesia, the Pitcairn Islands, Cook Islands, and Easter Island.
The red eel (Myroconger compressus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the West African coast, Cape Verde Islands, and Saint Helena.
The sand stargazer (Myxodagnus belone) is known only from a small number of specimens collected from two shallow water localities in the Bahamas and another in Puerto Rico.
The Chay torrent catfish (Nahangbagrus songamensis) is known only from six specimens collected from the Chay River.
The Tangail catfish (Nangra bucculenta) is known only from a small floodplain area between two large tributaries of the Ganges in central Bangladesh.
The reef-flat pipefish (Nannocampus weberi) is known only from a few specimens collected off Bali and Sumba in the Lesser Sunda Islands.
Reid's citharine (Nannocharax reidi) is known only from one or two localities in the upper Cross River drainage, but may perhaps be more widespread.
The Iberian pencil smelt (Nansenia iberica) is known only from four specimens collected from a small area of the western Mediterranean, between the Balearic Islands and the eastern coast of Spain.

The humpnose unicornfish (Naso tuberosus) is known only from a few specimens collected from coral reefs across the Indian Ocean (Mauritius, the Seychelles, Mozambique, Cocos Island and southwestern Australia).
The emperor tetra (Nematobrycon palmeri) is confined to the San Juan and Atrato river drainages of northwestern Colombia (Chocó department).
Franz's cusk-eel (Neobythites franzi) is known only from a few specimens collected in deep waters off Dunk Island, Queensland, within the Great Barrier Reef.
The splendid killifish (Neofundulus splendidus) is known only from a single temporary pool in eastern Bolivia (Santa Cruz department).
The tiger teddy (Neoheterandria elegans) is a small type of fish known only from the Truandó River.
The Boteli tetra (Neolebias gracilis) is known only from marshes along the Boteli River.
Philippe's tetra (Neolebias philippei) is known only from two widely-spaced localities within the middle Congo drainage (the Itimbiri and Tshuapa rivers).
Folgor's scorpionfish (Neomerinthe folgori) is known only from a few specimens collected along the western African coast off Mauritania, the Cape Verde Islands, and Namibia.
The Xiangzhou icefish (Neosalanx argentea) is known only from its original description in the 1930s from the city of Xiangzhou (Guangdong).
Herring's searsid (Normichthys herringi) is a type of deep-sea smelt known only from two specimens collected within the Arabian Sea.
The Nato sea-catfish (Notarius armbrusteri) is known only from six specimens collected from brackish waters along the southwestern coast of Colombia.
Eriksson's blind cusk-eel (Nybelinella erikssoni) is known only from a few specimens collected from great depths in the Atlantic and western Indian oceans.
The Juan Fernández silverside (Odontesthes gracilis) is a little-known type of freshwater and marine fish endemic to the Juan Fernández Islands.
McCosker's coral brotula (Ogilbia mccoskeri) is known only from a few coral reef localities in coastal Panama, including the San Blas Islands.
The Pegu longtail catfish (Olyra burmanica) is known only from a few old museum specimens collected from the Pegu Range.
The Indawgyi longtail catfish (Olyra horae) is known only from a few museum specimens originating from Lake Indawgyi.

Robert's combtooth blenny (Omobranchus robertsi) is known only from brackish mangrove creeks in south-central coastal Papua New Guinea, but may perhaps occur as well on the northeastern portion of the Cape York Peninsula in Australia.
Steinitz's combtooth blenny (Omobranchus steinitzi) is known only from four specimens collected from a single locality in the Dahlak Archipelago, in the southern Red Sea.
Clarke's dreamer (Oneirodes clarkei) is known only from the waters of the Madeira Islands.
The Na-Ri shovel-jaw carp (Onychostoma uniforme) is known only from the Na-Ri River.
The thin snake-eel (Ophichthus apachus) is known only from two specimens, the first collected near the Tres Marías Islands of Mexico and the second off the coast of western Colombia.
The Sicilian snake-eel (Ophichthus maculatus) is known only from a specimen collected in 1810 from the waters near Sicily.
The spotted snake-blenny (Ophiclinops pardalis) is confined to a small area of coastal South Australia.
The Vaqueria longfin herring (Opisthopterus effulgens) appears to be confined to estuarine environments in northwestern coastal Ecuador.
Smithvaniz's jawfish (Opistognathus smithvanizi) is known only from two specimens collected from Isla del Caño, off the southwestern coast of Costa Rica.
Walker's jawfish (Opistognathus walkeri) is known only from the central-western Gulf of California.
Leleup's salmon (Opsaridium leleupi) is known only from the upper Congo (Lualaba) River in southern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Ismailia tilapia (Oreochromis ismailiaensis) is a type of cichlid known only from the Ismailia Channel.
Delacour's bat-catfish (Oreoglanis delacouri) is known only from the upper Ngiap River.
The Xiangkhouang bat-catfish (Oreoglanis macronemus) is known only from four specimens collected in the mid 1920s from the Xiangkhouang Plateau of northern Laos.

The upper Mekong bat-catfish (Oreoglanis setiger) is known only from a few records in the upper Mekong in southwestern China (Yunnan) and the Ma Oun River in northwestern Laos (Louang Namtha province).
The Doi Tung bat-catfish (Oreoglanis suraswadii) is known only from two rocky forest streams near Doi Tung, northern Thailand.
The Mekong sharkminnow (Osteochilus brachynotopteroides) is known only from a small number of localities dispersed throughout the Mekong River drainage.
The Serokan sharkminnow (Osteochilus serokan) is known only from two localities in northwestern Sumatra (Aceh and Sumatera Utara provinces).
The short-jaw soldierfish (Ostichthys brachygnathus) is known only from a few specimens collected in deep waters off Guam and Saipan in the Mariana Islands.
The Menderes sportive loach (Oxynoemacheilus cinicus) is known only from a single imprecise type locality, most likely within the Buyuk Menderes drainage.
The golden killifish (Pachypanchax playfairii) is a fresh and brackish water species endemic to streams and ponds in the granitic Seychelles.
The Mekong eel-loach (Pangio longimanus) is known only from specimens collected in 1997 from the confluence of the Leuk and Gnong rivers in north-central Laos.
The Nan Kwe eel-loach (Pangio lumbriciformis) is known only from Nan Kwe stream near Myitkina in northern Myanmar.
The East Coast lampeye (Pantanodon stuhlmanni) is confined to the lower reaches of river and brooks in the coastal areas of southeastern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania, including salt pans.
Banarescu's loach (Parabotia banarescui) is confined to the middle reaches of the Yangtze in east-central China (Hubei).
Kailola's snapper (Paracaesio paragrapsimodon) is known only from two specimens collected off Pohnpei in the Caroline Islands and from southeastern New Guinea.
Randall's hawkfish (Paracirrhites bicolor) is known only from two specimens collected in shallow waters near Caroline Atoll, Kiribati, and another two from the Tuamotu Archipelago.
The blackspot conger eel (Paraconger macrops) is confined to shallow coastal waters of the Madeira Islands and the Azores in the eastern Atlantic.
Ladiges' shellear (Parakneria ladigesi) is known only from the Cuango and Lulua rivers.
The Lufira shellear (Parakneria lufirae) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Lufira River and its effluents.
The dara (Parakuhlia macrophthalmus) is a rare type of grunt confined to the coastal waters of western Africa from Senegal to Angola.
Schmitt's flounder (Paralichthys schmitti) is known only from the Juan Fernández Islands off the coast of Chile.
Krefft's snailfish (Paraliparis kreffti) is known only from the Scotia Sea in the South Atlantic and the Weddell Sea off Antarctica.
The Oregon snailfish (Paraliparis megalopus) is known only from the Cascadia and Tufts abyssal plains off the coast of Oregon, United States.
The North Atlantic Ridge snailfish (Paraliparis nigellus) is known only from three specimens collected from two localities.
The long-eared snailfish (Paraliparis obliquosus) is known only from the vicinity of the Crozet and Kerguelan islands.
The long-eared snailfish (Paraliparis operculosus) is known only from deep waters surrounding the Kerguelan Islands.
Matsura's filefish (Paramonacanthus matsuurai) is known only from two specimens washed up on Chichi Jima, in the Bonin Islands.
The San Miguel drum (Paranebris bauchotae) is known only from three specimens collected from the Gulf of San Miguel.
The Changping stone loach (Paranemachilus genilepis) is known only from a single subterranean river in south-central China (southern Guangxi).
The Cape Verde sandperch (Parapercis atlantica) is known only from a few specimens collected in shallow waters within the Cape Verde Islands.
The Vu Gia gudgeon (Parasqualidus maii) is known only from the Vu Gia River, where it is threatened by hydropower developments.
The beautiful characin (Parastremma pulchrum) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Becordó River.
Bleeker's cichlid (Paratilapia bleekeri) is known only from specimens collected during the nineteenth century from the Ikopa River.
The Cerberus wriggler goby (Paraxenisthmus cerberusi) is known only from seven specimens collected from Pulau and another from Fiji.
The Ha Giang catfish (Pareuchiloglanis rhabdurus) is known only from a small area of the Lo River.
The Atrato scrapetooth (Parodon atratoensis) is known only from the Neguá, Sucio and Truandó rivers, tributaries of the middle Atrato River.
Moffitt's goatfish (Parupeneus moffitti) is known only from the Mariana Islands.
Kreft's cod icefish (Patagonotothen kreffti) is known only from the Burdwood Bank.
Paxton's cardinalfish (Paxton concilians) is known only from four specimens collected from the waters surrounding the Montebello Islands in northwestern coastal Australia.
Cohen's pufferfish (Pelagocephalus coheni) is known only from two specimens collected from the waters around Norfolk Island.
The eel blenny (Peronedys anguillaris) is known only from a few museum specimens collected in disjunct areas of southeastern Australia.
The margined filefish (Pervagor marginalis) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Marquesas and Line Islands, but likely occurs as well on other nearby atolls.
The Cuanza mormyrid (Petrocephalus cunganus) is known only from the lower Cuanza River.
Keating's mormyrid (Petrocephalus keatingii) is known only from a few specimens collected from the White Nile between the Sobat confluence and Khartoum in the early twentieth century.
The Lukinda mormyrid (Petrocephalus squalostoma) is known only from the Lukinda and Luapula rivers in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Bleher's tetra (Phenacogrammus bleheri) is confined to a small tributary of the Bari River, itself a tributary of the Oubangui River.
The Kienké tetra (Phenacogrammus stigmatura) is confined to the Kienké River.
The longsnout no-line scorpionfish (Phenacoscorpius longirostris) is known only from two specimens collected from the Norfolk Island Ridge and the Lord Howe Rise.
The southern fraildisc clingfish (Pherallodiscus varius) is a type of intertidal goby known only from three collections in southwestern Mexico (Jalisco), the last one in 1972.

Bentley's mormyrid (Marcusenius bentleyi), Wagenia Falls whiptailed catfish (Phractura fasciata), Wagenia Rapids loach catfish (Dolichamphilius longiceps), and Wagenia Falls claroteid catfish (Amarginops platus) are all known only from Wagenia Falls, the last in the Stanley Falls cataract system.
The Kasai whiptailed catfish (Phractura macrura) is known only from the Uamba and Cuilo rivers in northeastern Angola.
The Baja flashlightfish (Phthanophaneron harveyi) is a bioluminescent species known only from four specimens collected off the lower Baja California Peninsula and the Gulf of California.
The ruby seadragon (Phyllopteryx dewysea) is known only from four specimens collected from two disjunct localities off the southwestern coast of Australia (Recherche Archipelago and Perth region).

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The Saint Helena codling (Physiculus helenaensis) is confined to the waters around Saint Helena.
Parin's codling (Physiculus parini) is confined to seamounts of the Sala y Gomez Ridge.
Braun's senator wrasse (Pictilabrus brauni) is known only from five specimens collected from a reef off      Cheyne's Beach, in southwestern Western Australia.
The Huallaga pimelodella catfish (Pimelodella montana) is known only from a small area of central-western Peru (Huánuco department).

The broad-spotted molly (Poecilia latipunctata) was historically confined to a small area of the Tamesí River, but has since been introduced into other drainages in Hidalgo, San Luis Potosí, Veracruz and Puebla states.
The Acandí molly (Poecilia mechthildae) is known only from three specimens collected from a single locality within the Acandí River drainage.
The black-spotted livebearer (Poeciliopsis turneri) is confined to the Purificación and Marabasco river drainages of southwestern Mexico (Jalisco).
The Maldives righteye flounder (Poecilopsetta albomaculata) is known only from a few specimens collected in the waters around the Maldives.
The Chari mormyrid (Pollimyrus guttatus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Chari River drainage.
The Mascarene seabream (Polysteganus mascarenensis) is known only from three specimens collected from the western Indian Ocean.
The Helena scorpionfish (Pontinus helena) is known only from a few specimens collected off the coast of Venezuela.
The backlash scorpionfish (Pontinus nigerimum) is known only from a few specimens collected from the southeastern coast of South Africa, the southern coast of Madagascar, and the Mascarenes.
The smalleye midshipman (Porichthys oculellus) is a type of toadfish is known only from a few records from coastal northwestern Colombia and southern Panama.
The ocellated toadfish (Porichthys oculofrenum) is known only from two specimens collected off the coast of northern Brazil and Venezuela.
The naked cusk-eel (Porogadus nudus) is known only from a few specimens collected from deep waters off Mauritania and Cape Verde.
The Cape Verde cusk-eel (Porogadus subarmatus) is known only from a few specimens collected from deep waters of the Cape Verde Rise.
The Suoi Rut barb (Poropuntius brevispinus) is known only from the Suoi Rut stream within the Black River drainage.
The Mae Klong barb (Poropuntius melanogrammus) is confined to the upper Mae Klong River and adjacent areas, where it is threatened by dam construction and habitat degradation.

Whitehead's sawtooth pellonuline (Potamothrissa whiteheadi) is a type of herring known only from a few specimens collected within the Hombo River (a tributary of the Luhoko River) and the Lindi / Tshopo tributary, both in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Cali Priapis fish (Priapichthys caliensis) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Cauca River drainage.
The Istmina killifish (Priapichthys nigroventralis) is known only from two specimens collected from the middle San Juan River.
The yellowtail sawtail (Prionurus chrysurus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the waters of the Lesser Sunda Islands.
The oblique butterflyfish (Prognathodes obliquus) is known only from Saint Paul Rocks.
The wrinkle-jaw snailfish (Prognatholiparis ptychomandibularis) is known only from a single individual collected near Seguam Island, in the Aleutian Islands.
Karmovskaya's eel (Promyllantor atlanticus) is a deepwater species known only from the coast of the Republic of Congo.
The fringed tube blenny (Protemblemaria perla) is known only from three specimens collected in 1990 from Isla del Rey, in the Pearl Islands of the Gulf of Panama.
The Great Meteor dragonet (Protogrammus sousai) is known only from a few specimens collected in the 1960s.
The Nkhotakota cichlid (Protomelas macrodon) is known only from two specimens collected from a single locality on the southwestern shore of the lake.
The spiny turbot (Psettodes bennettii) is a large type of flatfish confined to the West African continental shelf from Western Sahara to Guinea.
The thicktail catfish (Pseudecheneis crassicauda) is known only from the Mewa Khola River.
The Thuy Loan catfish (Pseudecheneis maurus) is known only from the Thuy Loan River.
The Giri catfish (Pseudecheneis suppaetula) is known only from the upper reaches of the Giri River.
The Toh Daeng catfish (Pseudeutropius indigens) is known only from the Toh Daeng peat swamp forest in southeastern peninsular Thailand (Narathiwat province).
The Samiria banjo catfish (Pseudobunocephalus quadriradiatus) is known only from a small area of north-central Peru (Loreto department).
Boehlke's toothless characin (Pseudochalceus bohlkei) is a type of freshwater fish known only from a small tributary of the Esmeraldas River.
Kyburz's toothless characin (Pseudochalceus kyburzi) is a little-known species confined to coastal rivers of western Colombia.
The western Indo-Pacific lined wrasse (Pseudocheilinus dispilus) is known only from eastern coastal Madagascar and off the islands of Mauritius and Réunion.
The Holmes Reefs wrasse (Pseudocoris aequalis) is known only from Holmes Reefs.
The San Blas coral brotula (Pseudogilbia sanblasensis) is known only from Chiriquí Lagoon and Morbeptopo Reef on the Caribbean coast of Panama.
The Mamoré armoured catfish (Pseudohemiodon thorectes) is known only from a few scattered localities within the Mamoré river drainage.
The Feni catfish (Pseudolaguvia inornata) is known only from the Koilla Khal creek, a tributary of the Feni River.
The bumblebee catfish (Pseudomystus bomboides) is is known only from three specimens collected in 1997 from the Leuk River.
The mottled flounder (Pseudorhombus binii) is known only from two disjunct coastal localities off southwestern Ecuador and northwestern Peru.
The Putao torrent minnow (Psilorhynchus brachyrhynchus) is known only from a few localities within the upper Irrawaddy River drainage of northern Myanmar.
The Ma Gawe torrent minnow (Psilorhynchus breviminor) is known only from the Ma Gawe River, a tributary of the Saman River.
Rahman's torrent minnow (Psilorhynchus rahmani) is known only from a single small hillstream located north of Chittagong in southeastern Bangladesh.
The blunt-snout goby (Psilotris amblyrhynchus) is known only from a few specimens collected in coastal Belize and Honduras.

The lowfin dartfish (Ptereleotris brachyptera) is known only from a handful of specimens collected from three, widely-separated fringing reef localities (coastal Borneo, Palau and the Marshall Islands).
Landon's tetra (Pterobrycon landoni) is known only from a few specimens collected within the lower and middle Atrato River drainage.
Ernest Magnus' cichlid (Ptychochromis ernestmagnusi) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Mananara du Nord River.
The Fort Dauphin cichlid (Ptychochromis mainty) is known only from forested streams in extreme southeastern Madagascar (former Toliara province).
