The Makira cichlid (Ptychochromis makira) is known only from two specimens collected from the Antainambalana River.
Kheel's trout barb (Raiamas kheeli) is known only from a few specimens collected from two, widely-separated localities in the lower Congo River, though it likely extends more widely.
The Sierra Leone trout barb (Raiamas scarciensis) is known only from the Little Scarcies River and the Waanje River of Sierra Leone and Guinea.
Gerlach's rasbora (Rasbora gerlachi) is known only from its initial collection in the 1920s from a single, undefined locality in Cameroon.
The Nanla rasbora (Rasbora septentrionalis) is confined to the Nanla and Youan rivers.
Lever's goby (Redigobius leveri) is known only from a few shallow freshwater creeks and rivers on Viti Levu, Vanua Levu and Taveuni.
The Ninigo combtooth blenny (Rhabdoblennius papuensis) is confined to shallow seaward reef flats in the          Ninigo Islands, off northern Papua New Guinea.

The blackish stumpnose (Rhabdosargus niger) is known only from a few frozen specimens obtained from a fish market in Busan, South Korea, said to have originated from somewhere off the southwestern coast of Borneo.
The cruel cichlid (Rhamphochromis ferox) is known only from a few specimens collected from Lake Malawi and the Shire River.
Nguyen's goby (Rhinogobius imfasciocaudatus) is known only from a few creeks and rivers in the mountains of northern Vietnam (Ha Giang and Lai Chau provinces).
The Nanla goby (Rhinogobius maculicervix) is confined to the Nanla and Youan rivers.
Miller's goby (Rhinogobius milleri) is known only from small creeks within the Nam Mat and Nam Mo river drainages of northeastern Laos.
The Bangkok goby (Rhinogobius vexillifer) is known only from streams and tributary rivers within the lower Chao Phraya drainage, in what is now the city of Bangkok.
Cea's scorpionfish (Rhinopias cea) is known only from two specimens collected from shallow waters off Eastern Island and Rapa, in French Polynesia.
Facciolà's morid cod (Rhynchogadus hepaticus) is known only from deep waters in the Gulf of Naples, the Strait of Messina, the Catalan Sea and off the Balearic Islands.
Wiener's drum (Robaloscion wiener) is known only from two specimens collected in the late nineteenth century from Callao Bay, off the coast of central Peru and another undefined locality off Chile.
Robin's goby (Robinsichthys arrowsmithensis) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Arrowsmith Bank.
McGrouther's flathead (Rogadius mcgroutheri) is known only from four specimens collected from the waters off northeastern Australia and New Caledonia.
Shen's righteye flounder (Samariscus filipectoralis) is known only from the South China Sea, where it may be threatened from overfishing and trawling bycatch.
The Bay of Bengal lizardfish (Saurida pseudotumbil) is known only from a few specimens collected from the eastern coast of India.
Day's goby (Scartelaos cantoris) is known only from three specimens collected in the Andaman Islands in the 1870s.
The yellowtail parrotfish (Scarus obishime) is confined to rocky and coral-encrusted slopes in the Bonin Islands.
The Dhofar parrotfish (Scarus zufar) is known only from rocky reefs off the coast of Oman.
The Cuanza butter catfish (Schilbe angolensis) is known only from the upper Cuanza River.
The sooty goby (Schismatogobius fuligimentus) is known only from a few streams in southern Grande Terre (Provence Sud), where it is threatened by nickel mining activities.
species.iucn: Schismatogobius fuligimentus Chen, Séret, Pöllabauer & Shao, 2001

species.e: The Espiritu Santo goby (Schismatogobius vanuatuensis) is confined to streams on Espiritu Santo.
The Hwe-gna-sang stone loach (Schistura acuticephala) is known only from the Hwe-gna-sang River, on the Shan Plateau of northern Myanmar (Shan State).
The Aramis stone loach (Schistura aramis) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Nua River.
The Bach Ma stone loach (Schistura bachmaensis) is known only from a single small stream within the Thua Luu River drainage.
The tri-banded stone loach (Schistura balteata) is known only from a small area of the southern Malay Peninsula (Myanmar and Thailand).
The Black River stone loach (Schistura callichromus) is known only from a single tributary in Yunnan, China, but may occur in other parts of the Black River drainage.
The Moei stone loach (Schistura moeiensis) is known only from four tributary streams within the Moei River drainage, but may be more widespread.
The Hwe-nga-sang stone loach (Schistura paucifasciata) is known only from its original description in 1929 from the Hwe-nga-sang River.
The Phong Tho stone loach (Schistura phongthoensis) is known only from a few creeks and rivers in northwestern Vietnam (Lai Chau province).
The Tengchong stone loach (Schistura polytaenia) is known only from a single tributary of the upper Irrawaddy in southwestern China (Yunnan).
The Bang Fai stone loach (Schistura punctifasciata) is confined to the Bang Fai River downstream of the subterranean section.

Walton's stone loach (Schistura waltoni) is confined to the Ping, Wang and Yom tributaries of the upper Chao Phraya drainage in northwestern Thailand, where it is threatened by habitat destruction and degradation.
The Sattar snowtrout (Schizothorax curvilabiatus) is confined to the lower reaches of the Tsangpo River.
Tsao's snowtrout (Schizothorax meridionalis) is known only from two tributaries of the upper Irrawaddy in southwestern China (Yunnan).
The Nujiang snowtrout (Schizothorax nukiangensis) is confined to the upper Salween River in Yunnan.
The Azores scorpionfish (Scorpaena azorica) is a rare species known only from the waters off Terceiera Island.
The bold scorpionfish (Scorpaena orgila) is known only from a few specimens collected from a shallow rocky reef near Easter Island.
The Messina scorpionfish (Scorpaenodes arenai) is known only from a few specimens collected off the Azores and from the Strait of Messina in the central Mediterranean.
The African large-spotted scorpionfish (Scorpaenodes elongatus) is known only from a handful os specimens collected off the coast of Senegal.
The pygmy scorpionfish (Scorpaenodes scaber) is known only from two specimens collected from Shark Reef, off southeastern Australia.
The Korean rockfish (Sebastes koreanus) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Yellow Sea.
The Gulf of California rockfish (Sebastes peduncularis) is known only from two specimens collected in the north-central Gulf of California.
The Nanla stone loach (Sectoria heterognathos) is confined to the Nanla and Youan rivers.
The Hiva Oa coastal stream goby (Stenogobius marqueti) and the Atuana goby (Sicyopterus marquesensis) are confined to Hiva Oa.
The Masoala goby (Sicyopterus punctissimus) is restricted to a few isolated localities on the Masoala Peninsula of northeastern Madagascar (former Antsiranana province), where it is uncommon.
The Cebu goby (Sicyopus cebuensis) is a freshwater and marine species known only from a few specimens collected from the Philippines, Taiwan, Java, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and southern Japan.
The Dumaguete goby (Silhouettea nuchipunctatus) is known only from a single tide pool on the island of Negros in the Philippines.

The silver-banded sillago (Sillago argentifasciata) is a smelt-like species confined to the Balabac Strait off the southern tip of Palawan in the Philippines, where it is likely threatened by fisheries activity.
The Ha Giang hillstream loach (Sinogastromyzon hagiangensis) is confined to small rivers and creeks within the Lo River drainage.
Southwell's pipefish (Siokunichthys southwelli) is known only from four specimens collected at two widely-separated localities (Marichchukkaddi Bay in Sri Lanka and Mindoro, Philippines).
The longtail weed whiting (Siphonognathus tanyourus) is known only from a few museum specimens collected off the southern coast of Australia.
Stanaland's sole (Solea stanalandi) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Persian Gulf.
Duncker's pipehorse (Solegnathus dunckeri) is confined to the waters of Lord Howe Island and the eastern coast of Australia (Queensland and New South Wales).
The Ganges seabream (Sparidentex datnia) is known only from the mouth of the Ganges River in northeastern India and Bangladesh.
The grey-red parrotfish (Sparisoma griseorubrum) is known only from a small area off the northern coast of Venezuela.
The Truandó whiptail catfish (Spatuloricaria atratoensis) is known only from a tributary of the Truandó River.
The Peruvian pufferfish (Sphoeroides andersonianus) is known only from a few specimens collected off the coast of Peru.
The plaincheek pufferfish (Sphoeroides georgemilleri) is known only from a few specimens collected off the coast of northwestern Colombia.
The Ionian barracuda (Sphyraena intermedia) is known only from the Gulf of Taranto in the Ionian Sea.

The Cortez barracuda (Sphyraena lucasana) is confined to the region of the Gulf of California, the Baja California Peninsula and coastal southwestern Mexico, where it is potentially threatened by overfishing.
The Thu Bon barb (Spinibarbus brevicephalus) is confined to the Thu Bon River.
The Ceyhan chub (Squalius seyhanensis) is known only from two localities within the upper Ceyhan River drainage.
Hasan's chub (Squalius spurius) is confined to the Orontes and Nahr al-Kabir river drainages of southeastern Turkey and northern Syria.
Hoese's blenny (Starksia hoesei) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Gulf of California and the western coast of Mexico (Guerrero) in 1975.
The scalybelly blenny (Starksia lepidogaster) is known only from a few specimens collected from rocky reefs off Cleopha Island, in the Marías Islands, in 1961.
The brown-spotted blenny (Starksia posthon) is known only from a few specimens collected disjunction from coastal southwestern Mexico and southern Panama.
Springer's blenny (Starksia springeri) is known only from four shallow reef localities in the southern Caribbean (Curaçao, Bonaire, Isla de Aves and Isla los Roques).
The M'pozo cichlid (Steatocranus mpozoensis) is known only from the mouth of the M'pozo River and from the opposite bank in the main Congo River.
The smallplate sculpin (Stelgistrum beringianum) is known only from a couple of specimens collected from around the Aleutian Islands in the early twentieth century.
The professor stardrum (Stellifer walkeri) is known only from a few specimens collected along the southwestern coast of Mexico from Nayarit to Guerrero.
The amigo stardrum (Stellifer wintersteenorum) is known only from a few specimens collected from the eastern Gulf of California.
The New Britain coastal stream goby (Stenogobius alleni) is known only from ten specimens collected from a small freshwater stream in northeastern New Britain.
The Nuku Hiva coastal stream goby (Stenogobius caudimaculosus) is confined to Nuku Hiva.
The Hiva Oa coastal stream goby (Stenogobius marqueti) and the Atuana goby (Sicyopterus marquesensis) are confined to Hiva Oa.
Randall's coastal stream goby (Stenogobius randalli) is confined to Tubuai.
The Ua Pou coastal stream goby (Stenogobius squamosus) is confined to Ua Pou.
Watson's coastal stream goby (Stenogobius watsoni) is known only from three islands in Milne Bay, southeastern New Guinea, where it lives in freshwater creeks.
The Matos catfish (Stenolicmus sarmientoi) is known only from four specimens collected from the Matos River.
The Sundaic knight goby (Stigmatogobius borneensis) is known only from a handful of specimens collected from brackish streams on Borneo.
The Vanuatu stiphodon (Stiphodon astilbos) is a type of freshwater goby known only from coastal streams on Santo, Pentecost and Efate islands.
The Samoan stiphodon (Stiphodon hydroreibatus) is a type of freshwater goby known only from a small number of specimens collected from the Samoan Islands and Futuna Islands.
Kalfatak's stiphodon (Stiphodon kalfatak) is a type of freshwater goby known only from eight specimens collected from the Namatia River.
Larson's stiphodon (Stiphodon larson) is a type of freshwater goby known only from a small area of northeastern Papua New Guinea and adjacent islands.
Russell's slender wrasse (Suezichthys russelli) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Gulf of Suez.
The clearspot flounder (Syacium maculiferum) is known only from a few specimens collected from the waters around Cocos Island.
Lubbock's tonguefish (Symphurus lubbocki) is a type of flatfish known only from two specimens collected off Ascension Island.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The reticulated tonguefish (Symphurus reticulatus) is a type of flatfish known only from a few specimens collected in shallow waters off Saint Helena.
The smooth handfish (Sympterichthys unipennis) was a type of anglerfish historically endemic to the coastal waters of Tasmania, where it appears to have been fairly common.
The Valdivia dragonet (Synchiropus valdiviae) is known only from three specimens collected from the Walvis Ridge off southwestern Africa and from Tristan da Cunha.
The Cortez pipefish (Syngnathus carinatus) is confined to estuarine habitats and beaches in the northern Gulf of California, where it is potentially threatened by coastal development.
The Hurghada pipefish (Syngnathus macrophthalmus) is confined to the northwestern Red Sea.

Both are threatened by trawl fisheries bycatch, habitat destruction and collection for the international aquarium trade, curios, and for “traditional medicine.” Makax's pipefish (Syngnathus makaxi) is confined to shallow seagrass habitats off the Yucatán Peninsula in southeastern Mexico.
The white-finned squeaker catfish (Synodontis caudovittatus) is known only from a few specimens collected from Ethiopia, South Sudan and Sudan during the early twentieth century.
The Stanley Pool squeaker catfish (Synodontis pulcher) is known only from two specimens collected from Stanley Pool.
Roberts' squeaker catfish (Synodontis robertsi) is a type of upside-down catfish known only from specimens collected in the Lukenie River, east-central Democratic Republic of Congo, in 1974.
Mundy's lizardfish (Synodus mundyi) is a bottom-dwelling species known only from two specimens collected near Oahu and from Penguin Bank, a submerged shield volcano.
Pyle's lizardfish (Synodus pylei) is known only from two specimens collected in deep waters around the Fiji Islands.
The Vietnamese cardinal minnow (Tanichthys micagemmae) is confined to the Ben Hai River.
The Cocos pufferfish (Tetraodon implutus) is known only from specimens collected in the 1830s from HMS Beagle survey near the Cocos Islands, southwest of Sumatra.
The Ascension wrasse (Thalassoma ascensionis) is confined to shallow waters off Ascension Island.
The slant-band wrasse (Thalassoma loxum) is known only from a few specimens collected in shallow waters off Oman and Socotra Island.

species.s: The Saint Helena Seamount Chain, also known as the Saint Helena Seamounts
species.e: The Saint Helena wrasse (Thalassoma sanctaehelenae) is known only from the waters around Saint Helena.
The seven-banded wrasse (Thalassoma septemfasciatum) is known only from a few historical records from Western coastal Australia, between Shark Bay and Perth.
The Fijian leatherjacket (Thamnaconus fijiensis) is a rare type of filefish known only from three specimens collected from Fiji, New Caledonia, and the Kii Peninsula of Honshu, Japan.
The Sanaga pygmy herring (Thrattidion noctivagus) is known only from a few specimens collected in 1972 from the lower Sanaga River.
The reticulated clingfish (Tomicodon lavettsmithi) is known only from shallow intertidal waters surrounding Pelican Cays and Twin Cays, on the coast of Belize.
The Ecuadorian clingfish (Tomicodon prodomus) is known only from two collections from southwestern Colombia and western Ecuador, the last of which was in 1970.
Tsukawaki's dragonet (Tonlesapia tsukawakii) is known only from a small area of the Tonlé Sap River.
The dwarf mahseer (Tor kulkarnii) is known only from four specimens collected from the Darna River in the early 1990s.
Randall's toadfish (Torquigener randalli) is a type of pufferfish confined to the waters off Oahu.
The Zamora pencil catfish (Trichomycterus bomboizanus) is known only from the Bomboiza and Gualaquiza rivers within the Santiago River drainage of southeastern Ecuador.
Taczanowski's pencil catfish (Trichomycterus taczanowskii) is known only from the Huambo and Tortora rivers in northwestern Peru.
The Philippine Sea pygmy goby (Trimma caudipunctatum) is known only from two specimens collected from the Ryukyu Islands and Palau along with a small number of obervations.
The spotted-cheek sole (Trinectes opercularis) is known only from a few specimens collected from shallow waters off southwestern Colombia and Ecuador.
The ornate characin (Trochilocharax ornatus) is known only from a single imported specimen originating from the city of Iquitos.
The elongated cichlid (Tylochromis elongatus) is confined to the upper Congo (Lualaba) River and Wagenia Falls.
The tidal cichlid (Tylochromis praecox) is known only from two localities in the tidal stretches of the lower Congo.
The Wintersteen drum (Umbrina wintersteeni) is known only from a few specimens collected along the southern coast of the Baja California Peninsula and in the southern Gulf of California.
Moutham's goatfish (Upeneus mouthami) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Chesterfield Bank.
The Vanuatu goatfish (Upeneus vanuatu) is known only from a few specimens collected in the deep waters around Espiritu Santo and Malo islands in Vanuatu.
The many-spotted moray eel (Uropterygius polystictus) is known only from a few records from the eastern Pacific (Gulf of California and the Galápagos Islands).
The orangebelly goby (Varicus marilynae) is known only from two specimens collected from the western Atlantic (northeastern Gulf of Mexico and eastern Florida).
The Yamur grunter (Variichthys jamoerensis) is confined to this single small lake.
The lemon goby (Vomerogobius flavus) is a rare species known only from a handful of widely-spaced localities in the Bahamas, Belize, and Honduras, where it favours steep coral reef drop-offs.
The pygmy possum wrasse (Wetmorella tanakai) is known only from three specimens collected over a wide area of Indonesia and the Philippines.
The Peruvian selema (Xenichthys rupestris) is confined to shallow coastal waters in southern Ecuador and Peru.
Loveridge's barb (Xenobarbus loveridgei) is known only from three specimens collected from off the southern shore of Lake Victoria in the 1920s.
The Laccadive eel (Xenomystax trucidans) is known only from a few specimens collected from deep waters in the Maldives and Laccadives.
The yellow swordtail (Xiphophorus clemenciae) is confined to streams and brooks within the upper Coatzacoalcos River drainage.
The Guinea snake-eel (Xyrias guineensis) is a deepwater species known only from a few specimens collected from deepwaters off the coast of West Africa.
The Easter Island razorfish (Xyrichtys koteamea) is known only from deep waters surrounding Easter Island.
The Nan Tong stone loach (Yunnanilus parvus) is known only from an imprecise type locality (a cave outlet) in southern China (Yunnan).
The Kinsuka loach catfish (Zaireichthys zonatus) is known only from two specimens collected from the rapids just below Stanley Pool in the 1960s.
The convict zebra sole (Zebrias captivus) is known only from two specimens collected off the coast of Bahrain.
Günther's sculpin (Zesticelus bathybius) is known only from five specimens collected within Tosa Bay, on the southern coast of Honshu, Japan.
The Honshu eelpout (Zoarchias neglectus) is an eel-like fish confined to tidepoools in a small area of eastern coastal Honshu, Japan.
The Pakaraima shield frog (Adelophryne patamona) is known only from Mount Wokomung and Mount Maringma in Guyana, but likely occurs as well in adjacent areas of northern Brazil (Roraima).
species.iucn: Adelophryne patamona MacCulloch, Lathrop, Kok, Minter, Khan & Barrio-Amorós, 2008

species.e: The Upemba leaf-folding frog (Afrixalus upembae) is known only from a small area of southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The Kaweshkar spiny-chest frog (Alsodes kaweshkari) is known only from two specimens, the first collected from Wellington Island off the coast of southwestern Chile and the other from the adjacent mainland in what is now Bernardo O'Higgins National Park.
The pine woods salamander (Ambystoma silvense) is known only from two, widely-separated localities (Durango and Chihuahua).
The Tay Con Linh cascade frog (Amolops iriodes) is known only from Mount Tay Con Linh II.

species.v: Alto del Buey poison dart frog
species.e: The Alto del Buey poison dart frog (Andinobates altobueyensis) is known only from the pre-montane forests of the Alto del Buey, where it has not been seen since the 1970s.
The beautiful screeching frog (Arthroleptis formosus) is known only from a small area of western Guinea.
species.iucn: Arthroleptis formosus Rödel, Kouamé, Doumbia & Sandberger, 2011

species.e: The Itombwe screeching frog (Arthroleptis hematogaster) is confined to the Itombwe and Kabobo highlands of east-central Democratic Republic of Congo.
Loveridge's screeching frog (Arthroleptis loveridgei) is known only from two specimens collected in the Ituri Forest in 1925.
The Wondiwoi callulops frog (Asterophrys pullifer) is known only from the eastern slopes of the Wondiwoi Mountains.
The Antado stubfoot toad (Atelopus galactogaster) is known only from two localities within Paramillo National Park.
The Sira stubfoot toad (Atelopus siranus) is known only from a few specimens collected on the eastern slopes of the Sira Range.
Archbold's land frog (Austrochaperina archboldi) is known only from a type series collected in the Kratke Mountains.
The Victoria land frog (Austrochaperina brevipes) is known only from Mount Victoria and Myola Guest House in the Owen Stanley Mountains.
The pygmy land frog (Austrochaperina minutissima) is known only from two localities within the Wondiwoi Mountains.
Parker's land frog (Austrochaperina parkeri) is known only from three localities in southeastern coastal Papua New Guinea.
The Tafa Papua frog (Barygenys cheesmanae) is known only from Mount Tafa.
The yellow-throated Papua frog (Barygenys flavigularis) is known only from a small area of eastern Papua New Guinea.
The black-headed climbing salamander (Bolitoglossa nigrescens) is confined to a small area of Cartago province.
Kemp's toad (Bufoides kempi) is known only from two specimens collected before 1919 from the Garo Hills.
The warty callulops frog (Callulops glandulosus) is known only from Mount Kerewa, in central Papua New Guinea.
The Crater Mountains callulops frog (Callulops marmoratus) is known only from specimens collected in the vicinity of the Crater Mountain Biological Station.
The Star Mountains callulops frog (Callulops sagittatus) is known only from two localities within the Star Mountains.
species.iucn: Callulops sagittatus Richards, Burton, Cunningham & Dennis, 1995

species.e: The Napo horned frog (Ceratophrys testudo) is confined to a single locality in central Ecuador (Napo province).
Bokermann's humming frog (Chiasmocleis centralis) is known only from two localities in Goiás state.
The spotted foam-nest tree frog (Chiromantis punctatus) is known only from the southwestern foothills of the Arakan Mountains.
species.iucn: Chiromantis punctatus (Wilkinson, Win, Thin, Lwin, Shein & Tun, 2003)

species.e: Allison's narrow-mouthed frog (Choerophryne allisoni) is known only from a few specimens collected on Mount Sisa.
The Bahia aquatic caecilian (Chthonerpeton exile) is known only from a single (now lost) specimen collected from somewhere in eastern Brazil (Bahia).
The Menawa rainforest frog (Cophixalus bewaniensis) is known only from two specimens collected from Mount Menawa in the Bewani Mountains.
The Halmahera rainforest frog (Cophixalus montanus) is known only from a small area of northern Halmahera.
The pretty rainforest frog (Cophixalus pulchellus) is known only from Mount Hunstein.
The Tagula rainforest frog (Cophixalus tagulensis) is known only from three specimens and has not been reported since 1956.
The Wondiwoi rainforest frog (Cophixalus tridactylus) is known only from the eastern slopes of the Wondiwoi Mountains.

The Betsileo cophyline tree frog (Cophyla cowanii) is known only from a few specimens collected during the nineteenth century from an undefined locality in east-central Madagascar (former Toamasina and Fianarantsoa provinces).
The Tchabal Mbabo caecilian (Crotaphatrema tchabalmbaboensis) is known only from three specimens collected in 1997 from Mount Tchabal Mbabo, Cameroon (Adamawa region).
Battersby's yellow tree frog (Dendropsophus battersbyi) is known only from two specimens collected in 1800 from what is now the city of Caracas, in northern Venezuela.
The Wadi al Khalili toad (Duttaphrynus scorteccii) appears to be confined to Wadi al Khalili, located on a high plateau near Mafhaq in western Yemen.
The Malí fringe-limbed tree frog (Ecnomiohyla thysanota) is known only from Mount Malí.
The Parambikulam frog (Fejervarya parambikulamana) is known only from a now-lost holotype collected from what is now the Parambikulam Wildlife Sanctuary.
The San Alberto marsupial frog (Gastrotheca carinaceps) is known only from Yanachaga-Chemillén National Park.
species.iucn: Gastrotheca carinaceps Duellman, Trueb and Lehr, 2006

species.e: The Goa caecilian (Gegeneophis goaensis) is known only from three specimens collected in southwestern India (Goa).
species.iucn: Gegeneophis goaensis Bhatta, Dinesh, Prashanth & Kulkarni, 2007

species.e: The Jinxiu foam-nest tree frog (Gracixalus jinxiuensis) is known only from a few widely-scattered montane localities in southern China (southeastern Yunnan, northeastern Guangxi and southern Hunan) and northern Vietnam (Mount Fan Si Pan).
species.iucn: Gracixalus jinxiuensis (Hu in Hu, Fei & Ye, 1978)

species.e: The Victoria caecilian (Herpele multiplicata) is known only from a now-lost type specimen collected in southwestern Cameroon in 1912.
The Zhaoping tree frog (Hyla zhaopingensis) is known only from a small area in south-central China (eastern Guangxi).
The Irrawaddy golden-backed frog (Hylarana margariana) is known only from two specimens collected in 1875 on the Myanmar / southern China border.
The Sumatran golden-backed frog (Hylarana persimilis) is known only from two specimens collected from northeastern Sumatra (Sumatera Utara province).
Betancur's rocket frog (Hyloxalus betancuri) is known only from Paramillo National Park.

The Turkestanian salamander (Hynobius turkestanicus) is known only from a few specimens collected in 1909 from an imprecise locality in central Asia, but thought to be somewhere in eastern Uzbekistan or southern Kyrgyzstan.
Friedemann's reed frog (Hyperolius friedemanni) is known only from two localities on the shores of Lake Malawi (Karonga and Monkey Bay).
The Shaba reed frog (Hyperolius kibarae) is known only from the highlands of Upemba National Park.
The Omaniundu reed frog (Hyperolius sankuruensis) is known only from swamps and marshes in south-central Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Mae Wang Valley caecilian (Ichthyophis acuminatus) is known only from the Mae Wang Valley in northwestern Thailand (Chiang Mai province).
The Mahakkam caecilian (Ichthyophis asplenius) is known only from two localities in southwestern Sarawak (Malaysia).
The Dulit caecilian (Ichthyophis dulitensis) is confined to Mount Dulit.
The Abungabung caecilian (Ichthyophis glandulosus) is known only from western Mindanao and Basilan in the southern Philippines.
The Doi Suthep caecilian (Ichthyophis youngorum) is known only from a handful of adult and larval specimens collected in 1957 from a small forested valley.
The Makamunu Assumbo caecilian (Idiocranium russeli), one of the smallest of all caecilians, is known only from two localities in western Cameroon, but may perhaps occur more widely.
The reticulated frog (Ingerana reticulata) is known only from a small area of southeastern Tibet.
The Great Natuna sticky frog (Kalophrynus bunguranus) is known only from a few specimens.
Robinson's sticky frog (Kalophrynus robinsoni) is known only from Mount Tahan, where it was last reported in 1922.
The Waza running frog (Kassina wazae) is known only from a single ephemeral marsh within seasonally flooded grassland near Waza, in northern Cameroon.
Laura Miriam's ditch frog (Leptodactylus lauramiriamae) is known only from a single cerrado enclave in south-central Brazil (Rondônia).
Heyer's ditch frog (Leptodactylus pascoensis) is known only from three disjunct localities in central Peru.
The Gbanga forest tree frog (Leptopelis bequaerti) is known only from two widely-separated localities in Liberia.
The Virunga forest tree frog (Leptopelis fenestratus) is known only from the Semliki sector of the Virunga Mountains in Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Quissange forest tree frog (Leptopelis marginatus) is known only from a single (now lost) specimen collected in 1895 from Benguela province.
The Khammouane wart frog (Limnonectes khammonensis) is known only from the Khammouane Plateau in central Laos, near the border with Vietnam.
The Basilan wart frog (Limnonectes micrixalus) is now confined to Basilan, though it may have formerly occurred on Mindanao as well.
Lemos-Espinal's leopard frog (Lithobates lemosespinali) is a semi-aquatic species confined to two small areas in the northern Sierra Madre Occidental (southwestern Chihuahua).
The Biak frog (Litoria biakensis) is known only from two localities on Biak.
The four-lined frog (Litoria quadrilineata) is known only from a small area of southern coastal New Guinea (Papua province, Indonesia).

The yellow-spotted big-headed frog (Lynchius flavomaculatus) is known only from a few localities in southeastern Ecuador (Loja, Napo, Morona Santiago and Zamora Chinchipe provinces) and northwestern Peru (Huancabamba department).
The Barbacoas poison dart frog (Mannophryne larandina) is known only from a small area of Lara state.
The Ambohimitombi Madagascar frog (Mantidactylus ambohimitombi) is known only from a small area of montane grassland in east-central Madagascar (former Antananarivo province).
The Wawu horned frog (Megophrys wawuensis) is confined to Mount Wawu.
The Nairobi toad (Mertensophryne nairobiensis) is confined to a small area of savanna woodland in south-central Kenya.
Schmidt's toad (Mertensophryne schmidti) is known only from Upemba National Park.
The worm-patterned caecilian (Mimosiphonops vermiculatus) is known only from a few specimens collected in southeastern Brazil (Rio de Janeiro).
The Kakhien Hills tiny frog (Nanorana feae) is known only from the Kakhien Hills.
The Rara Lake tiny frog (Nanorana rarica) is confined to a small area of northwestern Nepal.
The Amani tree toad (Nectophrynoides frontierei) is known only from the Amani Nature Reserve in the East       Usambaras.
The Jerai odorous frog (Odorrana monjerai) is confined to montane streams and their environs on Mount Jerai.
The false Cienega Colorado worm salamander (Oedipina pseudouniformis) is confined to four widely scattered pockets of both montane and lowland forest in Costa Rica and Nicaragua.

Stuart's worm salamander (Oedipina stuarti) is known only from two specimens said to have originated on Tigre Island, though it is possible that they actually came from somewhere on the Honduran mainland.
The black-throated cross frog (Oreophryne atrigularis) is known only from two disjunct localities in the region of the Vogelkop Peninsula (Papua Barat and Papua provinces, Indonesia).
The Ayanganna bush toad (Oreophrynella dendronastes) is known only from the northeastern plateau of Mount Ayanganna.
The Joinville caecilian (Oscaecilia hypereumeces) is known only from two specimens collected at a single locality in southeastern Brazil (Santa Catarina).

The Maolan salamander (Paramesotriton maolanensis) is known only from a single deep pool in the Maolan National Nature Reserve in southeastern China (Guizhou), where it probably also lives in underground rivers.
species.iucn: Paramesotriton maolanensis Gu, Chen, Tian, Li & Ran, 2012

species.e: Largen's puddle frog (Phrynobatrachus inexpectatus) is known only from three scattered localities within the Ethiopian Highlands.
The green-eyed tree frog (Polypedates chlorophthalmus) is known only from Mount Murud.
The Damaraland pygmy toad (Poyntonophrynus damaranus) is confined to the Kaokoveld Desert.
The Tobago robber frog (Pristimantis turpinorum) is known only from a few localities in northeastern Tobago.
The hot springs ridged frog (Ptychadena filwoha) is known only from two closely-adjacent springs and pools within the northern Rift Valley of Ethiopia.
Wade's ridged frog (Ptychadena wadei) is known only from a small area of the Northeastern Highlands.
The Sangir gliding tree frog (Rhacophorus rhyssocephalus) is confined to Great Sangir.
Baumgardner's snouted tree frog (Scinax baumgardneri) is known only from a few specimens collected in southern Venezuela (Amazonas state).
The Monogaga toad (Sclerophrys danielae) is known only from a small area of wouthwestern coastal Ivory Coast, where it was last recorded in the late 1970s.
The Djohong toad (Sclerophrys djohongensis) is known only from the Adamawa Plateau in north-central Cameroon, though it may occur as well in adjacent areas of southeastern Nigeria.
The Langano toad (Sclerophrys langanoensis) is known only from the northern Rift Valley of Ethiopia, where it has been recorded from Lake Langano and from Awash National Park.
The Turkana toad (Sclerophrys turkanae) is known only from the southeastern shores of Lake Turkana and from near the Ewaso Ng'iro River in northern and central Kenya.
The banded toad (Sclerophrys vittata) is a little-known species confined to marshy areas in Uganda.
The Qanning lazy toad (Scutiger brevipes) is known only from Mount Qanning.
The Wattakole burrowing frog (Sphaerotheca leucorhynchus) is known only from a single (now lost) specimen collected from Karnataka in the 1930s.
The red land frog (Sphenophryne rubra) is known only from a few specimens collected in east-central Papua New Guinea.
The Taracuna robber frog (Strabomantis laticorpus) is known only from Mount Tacarcuna and Mount Malí.
Megson's stump-toed frog (Stumpffia megsoni) is known only from a few small caves in far northern coastal Madagascar (former Antsiranana province).
species.iucn: Stumpffia megsoni Köhler, Vences, D'Cruze & Glaw, 2010

species.e: Hall's water frog (Telmatobius halli) was long known only from a few specimens collected in 1935 from a high-elevation hot spring in northern Chile (Antofagasta region).
The Alexandria frog (Uperoleia orientalis) is known only from a few specimens collected in 1940 from a swamp in north-central Northern Territory.
Gans' caecilian (Uraeotyphlus gansi) is known only from the Kalakkad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve in Tamil Nadu.
species.iucn: Uraeotyphlus gansi Gower, Rajendran, Nussbaum & Wilkinson, 2008

species.e: The Chengalam caecilian (Uraeotyphlus interruptus) is a fossorial amphibian known only from a few specimens collected from a rubber plantation in southwestern India (Kerala).
The Madinika Madagascar frog (Wakea madinika) is known only from specimens collected in 2001 from a temporary pond on a cacao plantation in northeastern Madagascar (former Antsiranana province).
The Ugandan clawed frog (Xenopus ruwenzoriensis) is known only from two localities in western Uganda.
The Star Mountains fanged frog (Xenorhina anorbis) is known only from two localities within the Star Mountains.
The Papuan swiftlet (Aerodramus papuensis) is known only from a handful of specimens collected over a wide area of northern and eastern New Guinea.
The Luzon Whitehead's swiftlet (Aerodramus whiteheadi whiteheadi) is confined to the mountains of Luzon.
Sillem's rosefinch (Carpodacus sillemi) was long known only from two specimens collected in 1929 from southern Xinjiang, China.
The blue-throated lorikeet (Charmosyna toxopei) is confined to Buru, where it is known only from a few specimens and rarely observed.

Prigogine's greenbul (Chlorocichla prigoginei) is a type of passerine bird known only from a few high-elevation localities in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where it is seriously threatened by habitat destruction.
The Tana River cisticola (Cisticola restrictus) is a passerine bird known only from a small number of specimens, all collected within the lower Tana River drainage.
The dusky tetraka (Crossleyia tenebrosa) is a rare type of warbler confined to eastern and northeastern Madagascar (former Antsiranana and Toamasina provinces).
The white-fronted swift (Cypseloides storeri) is an enigmatic species known only from a few specimens and sight records originating in southwestern Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, and Jalisco).
species.iucn: Cypseloides storeri Navarro, Peterson, Escalante & Benitez D., 1992

species.e: The coppery thorntail (Discosura letitiae) is a type of hummingbird known only from two specimens collected during the mid-nineteenth century from an unknown locality in Bolivia.
The black-lored waxbill (Estrilda nigriloris) is a type of finch restricted to the area of the Lualaba River and Lake Upemba in the southern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Enggano hill myna (Gracula enganensis) is confined to Enganno.
The brown-banded rail (Lewinia mirifica) is known only from Luzon, where it is subjected to heavy hunting.

Friedmann's lark (Mirafra pulpa) is a rare species known only from a small number of specimens collected in three disjunct areas of central and southern Kenya, southwestern Ethiopia, and northeastern Tanzania.
The Itombwe flycatcher (Muscicapa itombwensis) is confined to a narrow band of montane forest within the Itombwe Mountains.
The sombre rockchat (Oenanthe dubia) is a passerine bird known only from the highlands of east-central Ethiopia and northwestern Somalia.
The Norfolk Island ground dove (Pampusana norfolkensis) is known only from a single painting.
Hose's partridge (Rhizothera dulitensis) is known only from specimens collected during the nineteenth century from Mount Dulit and Mount Batu Song in Sarawak and from Mount Kinabalu in Sabah.

The little paradise kingfisher (Tanysiptera hydrocharis) is a rare species known only from a small number of localities in southern coastal New Guinea, the Aru Islands in the Moluccas, and possibly from islands in the Torres Strait.
The Luzon buttonquail (Turnix worcesteri) is known only from a few localities.
The Seram masked owl (Tyto almae) was first described in 2013, and known only from a couple of records.
The Rubeho forest partridge (Xenoperdix obscuratus) is confined to the Rubeho Mountains.
The ocellated guitarfish (Acroteriobatus ocellatus) is known only from a few specimens collected in coastal waters from southern Mozambique to southwestern South Africa.
The roughskin bullray (Aetomylaeus asperrimus) is known only from the southern coast of Panama and from the Galápagos Islands.
The whiteleg skate (Amblyraja taaf) appears to be largely confined to the waters of the Crozet and Kerguelan Islands.
The abyssal skate (Bathyraja ishiharai) is known only from two specimens collected at 2,300 metres depth on the Naturalist Plateau.
The small-spined deep-sea skate (Brochiraja microspinifera) is confined to the eastern coast of North Island, New Zealand.
The Arabian catshark (Bythaelurus alcockii) is known only from a single (now lost) specimen collected off the coast of Pakistan.
The broadhead catshark (Bythaelurus clevai) is known only from a few specimens collected from deep waters off the coast of southwestern Madagascar.
The western gulper shark (Centrophorus westraliensis) is a deepwater species endemic to southwestern Australia, from Shark Bay to Cape Leeuwin.
Cook's swellshark (Cephaloscyllium cooki) is restricted to a small area of the Arafura Sea, where it is known only from a few specimens.
Owston's chimaera (Chimaera owstoni) is known only from a few specimens collected in deep waters off eastern Honshu, Japan.

The southern mandarin dogfish (Cirrhigaleus australis) is known only from the coastal waters of southeastern Australia including Tasmania, and from northern New Zealand, but may perhaps be more wide-ranging.
The barbelthroat carpetshark (Cirrhoscyllium expolitum) is known only from two specimens collected from the northern South China Sea and the Gulf of Tonkin.
The smoothnose legskate (Cruriraja durbanensis) is known only from two specimens collected off the western coast of South Africa.
The pygmy thornback skate (Dentiraja flindersi) is known only from Investigator Strait and Backstairs Passage, off the coast of Kangaroo Island, South Australia.
The Ecuadorian skate (Dipturus ecuadoriensis) is known only from San Helena Bay off the coast of central Ecuador.
The Queensland deepwater skate (Dipturus queenslandicus) is known only from the Saumarez Plateau.
The Madagascar pygmy skate (Fenestraja maceachrani) is known only from a few deepwater localities off northwestern Madagascar.
The Siboga pygmy skate (Fenestraja sibogae) is a deepwater species known only from a few specimens.
The sailback houndshark (Gogolia filewoodi) is a distinctive-looking species known only from a single pregnant female taken by hand line in deep water off a river mouth in Papua New Guinea.
The Oman bullhead shark (Heterodontus omanensis) is known only from two localities off Pakistan and Masirah Island, Oman.
The Eilat sleeper ray (Heteronarce bentuviai) is a rare, deepwater species known only from the Gulf of Aqaba.
The soft electric ray (Heteronarce mollis) is a rare species known only from a few specimens collected from the northern Indian Ocean off Yemen, Somalia and southern India.
The eastern looseskin skate (Insentiraja laxipella) is known only from a very small area off Cairns in northeastern Australia (Queensland), where it likely occurs on seamounts.
The western Australian round skate (Irolita westraliensis) is confined to a small stretch of outer continental shelf off Western Australia, where it is threatened by trawling activity.
The tiger-tail rough skate (Leucoraja compagnoi) is known only from a few specimens collected off the western coast of South Africa.
The Madagascar electric ray (Narcine insolita) is known only from coastal southwestern Madagascar.
The bigeye electric ray (Narcine oculifera) is known only from the Sea of Oman and the Gulf of Aden.
The sapphire skate (Notoraja sapphira) is known only from the Norfolk Ridge.
McMillan's catshark (Parmaturus macmillani) is a small, rare and little-known species endemic to the deep waters of the lower continental slope around New Zealand.
The ocellated river stingray (Potamotrygon ocellata) is confined to the Amazon delta.
The Cape Verde skate (Raja herwigi) is apparently confined to the shelf off Boa Vista and São Vicente islands.
The Azores dogfish (Scymnodalatias garricki) is known only from a specimen collected from a seamount on the North Atlantic Ridge, and another collected south of the Azores.
Sherwood's dogfish (Scymnodalatias sherwoodi) is known only from five specimens, two collected in Australian waters (southwestern Australia and Tasmania) and the other off southeastern New Zealand.
The blue legskate (Sinobatis caerulea) is known only from a small area off the coast of Western Australia between       Dirk Hartog Island to the North West Cape.
The eastern legskate (Sinobatis filicauda) is known only from a few specimens collected from two small areas off northeastern Australia (the Queensland Plateau and part the Saumarez Plateau).
The bighead spurdog (Squalus bucephalus) is a small dogfish known only from a few specimens collected around seamounts of the Norfolk Ridge off Grande Terre, New Caledonia.
The Luzon broad-toothed rat (Abditomys latidens) is confined to central and northern Luzon (Laguna and Mountain provinces).
The Mersin spiny mouse (Acomys cilicicus) is known only from a small area of coastal rocky scrubland in southern Anatolia, Turkey.
Porter's rock rat (Aconaemys porteri) is confined to a small area of south-central Chile (Araucanía, Los Ríos and Los Lagos regions) and southwestern Argentina (Neuquén and Río Negro provinces).
The Chirinda veld rat (Aethomys silindensis) is known only from three localities within the Eastern Highlands.
The São Paulo grass mouse (Akodon sanctipaulensis) is known only from a few localities in São Paulo state.
Firouz's jerboa (Allactaga firouzi) is known only from a few areas of montane steppe in west-central Iran (Isfahan province).
The four-toed jerboa (Allactaga tetradactyla) is a hopping rodent confined to northern coast of Egypt and Libya, where it is threatened by habitat destruction.
The Somali gerbil (Ammodillus imbellis) is known only from a few specimens collected from Somalia and southeastern Ethiopia.
The Ucayali water rat (Amphinectomys savamis) is a semi-aquatic species known only from two localities in eastern Peru (Loreto department).
The giant mole shrew (Anourosorex schmidi) is known only from a few specimens collected on the southeastern slopes of the Himalayas in Bhutan and northeastern India (Arunachal Pradesh and Sikkim).
Hernández-Camacho's night monkey (Aotus jorgehernandezi) is a nocturnal species known only from a small area of the Cordillera Occidental in northwestern Colombia (Chocó department).
The greater lowland forest mouse (Apomys littoralis) is known only from the coastal plain of central Minadanao.
The mountain water rat (Baiyankamys habbema) is known only from a small area between Lake Habbema and Mount Wilhelmina in west-central New Guinea (Papua province, Indonesia).
The grey-bellied akodont (Brucepattersonius griserufescens) is a type of rodent known only from a few specimens collected from southeastern Brazil (Minas Gerais, Espírito Santo and Rio de Janeiro).
The soricine akodont (Brucepattersonius soricinus) is a type of rodent known only from a few specimens collected over a relatively wide area of southeastern Brazil (São Paulo and Paraná).
The Alborz brush-tailed mouse (Calomyscus grandis) is confined to montane forests of the Alborz Mountains.
Tsolov's mouse-like hamster (Calomyscus tsolovi) is known only from a small number of specimens said to have been collected in southwestern Syria.

The Campo-Ma'an fruit bat (Casinycteris campomaanensis) is known only from two specimens collected in the vicinity of Campo-Ma'an National Park, Cameroon (South region), and a possible third in neighbouring Nigeria.
The Sichuan dormouse (Chaetocauda sichuanensis) is known only from five specimens collected from the mountains of central China (northern Sichuan).

Dalquest's pocket mouse (Chaetodipus dalquesti) is confined to “foggy desert” areas on the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula (Baja California Sur), where it is seriously threatened by tourism development.
The lined pocket gopher (Chaetodipus lineatus) is confined to a small area of Zacatecas and San Luis Potosi.
Groves' dwarf lemur (Cheirogaleus grovesi) is known only from a few specimens collected within Ranomafana and Andringitra national parks (former Toamasina, Antananarivo and Fianarantsoa provinces).
species.iucn: Cheirogaleus grovesi McLain, Lei, Frasier, Taylor, Bailey, Robertson, Nash, Randriamanana, Mittermeier & Louis Jr, 2017

species.e: The Palawan pencil-tailed tree mouse (Chiropodomys calamianensis) is confined to lowland forests on Palawan, the Calamian Islands, and Balabac.

The grey-bellied pencil-tailed tree mouse (Chiropodomys muroides) is known only from a few specimens collected from Mount Kinabalu in northern Borneo (Sabah, Malaysia) and at another locality in eastern Borneo (Kalimantan Timur, Indonesia).
The lesser Taiwanese shrew (Chodsigoa sodalis) is known only from five specimens collected from montane forest.
The Baturité prehensile-tailed porcupine (Coendou baturitensis) is a little-known species confined to the Baturité Mountains.
The brown prehensile-tailed porcupine (Coendou vestitus) is known only from a few specimens collected from two localities in west-central Colombia (Cundinamarca and Tolima departments).
The Dhofar shrew (Crocidura dhofarensis) is known only from two shrubby localities in Oman and Yemen.
The heather shrew (Crocidura erica) is known only from western Angola.
Fischer's shrew (Crocidura fischeri) is known only from two localities in southern Kenya and northeastern Tanzania.
The greater Mindanao shrew (Crocidura grandis) was long known only from two specimens recorded from Mount Malindang in 1906.
The savanna swamp shrew (Crocidura longipes) is known only from two small and isolated swamps near Lake Kainji, in northwestern Nigeria (Kebbi state).
The Mindoro shrew (Crocidura mindorus) is thought to be confined to the higher elevations of Mount Halcon in north-central Mindoro.
The Egyptian pygmy shrew (Crocidura religiosa) is known only from two specimens, one collected from the neck of the Nile delta and the other from further down the Nile.
The Tarfaya shrew (Crocidura tarfayensis) is confined to southern Morocco and northern Mauritania.
The Timor shrew (Crocidura tenuis) is confined to Timor.
Zimmer's shrew (Crocidura zimmeri) is known only from two specimens collected from Upemba National Park in 1936.
Agricola's gracile mouse opossum (Cryptonanus agricolai) is known only from very few records over a wide area of eastern Brazil.
The Guahiba gracile mouse opossum (Cryptonanus guahybae) is known only from a few localities in southeastern Brazil (Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina and Paraná).

The Cundinamarca small-footed shrew (Cryptotis brachyonyx) is known only from four specimens collected from two localities in west-central Colombia (Cundinamarca department), the most recent record being from 1925.
The Honduran small-eared shrew (Cryptotis hondurensis) is known only from a small area of south-central Honduras (Francisco Morazán department).
The Oaxacan broad-clawed shrew (Cryptotis peregrina) is known only from two localities in western Oaxaca.
The Peruvian small-eared shrew (Cryptotis peruviensis) is known only from two specimens collected from high-elevation elfin forest in northwestern Peru (Cajamarca department).

Val's gundi (Ctenodactylus vali) is a type of rodent confined to two small, widely separated areas in North Africa, the first in northeastern Morocco and northwestern Algeria, and the other in northwestern Libya.
Knight's tuco-tuco (Ctenomys knighti) is a type of burrowing rodent confined to a small area of montane grassland in northwestern Argentina (Catamarca and La Rioja provinces).
The Machu Picchu arboreal chinchilla rat (Cuscomys oblativa) is a cat-sized species long known only from two skulls collected from an Inca burial site in 1912 in southeastern Peru (Cusco department).
The montane bamboo rat (Dactylomys peruanus) is known only from two widely separated localities in southeastern Peru (Puno department) and western Bolivia (La Paz department).
Fox's shaggy rat (Dasymys foxi) is confined to the central Jos Plateau.
The hairy long-nosed armadillo (Dasypus pilosus) is known only from a few localities in western Peru (San Martín, La Libertad, Huánuco, Junín and Amazonas departments).
Rupp's climbing mouse (Dendromus ruppi) is known only from the Imatong Mountains.
The velvet African climbing mouse (Dendroprionomys rousseloti) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Zoological Garden of Brazzaville, in southeastern Republic of Congo.
The Umnak collared lemming (Dicrostonyx unalascensis) is confined to the islands of Umnak and Unalaska.
Crump's mouse (Diomys crumpi) is known only from a few widely-separated localities in northern India (Bihar and Manipur), southern Nepal, and northern Myanmar.
The arboreal soft-furred spiny rat (Diplomys caniceps) is known only from a small area of the Cauca River Valley in Antioquia department.

Pousargues' mongoose (Dologale dybowskii) is known only from a small number of specimens collected in eastern Central Africa Republic, northern Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and southern South Sudan.
The woolly dormouse (Dryomys laniger) is largely confined to the Taurus Mountains of southern Anatolia, Turkey, along with a few isolated localities in northeastern Anatolia.
Vieira's spiny tree rat (Echimys vieirai) is known only from two localities south of the Amazon River in central Brazil (Amazonas and Pará).
The dusky elephant shrew (Elephantulus fuscus) is known only from a handful of specimens collected from southern Zambia, Malawi, and southwestern Mozambique.

The tsingy tuft-tailed rat (Eliurus antsingy) is known only from a few specimens collected in disjunct areas of limestone tsingy forests and other formations in western Madagascar (former Mahajanga province).
The Alay mole vole (Ellobius alaicus) is known only from a small area of high-elevation meadow steppe in the Alay Mountains, south Kyrgyzstan.
Ansell's epauletted fruit bat (Epomophorus anselli) is known only from Malawi, where it has been collected in Kasungu National Park in the 1980s, and from the Karonga area in 1961.
The lesser Angolan epauletted fruit bat (Epomophorus grandis) is known only from three specimens collected in the mid-twentienth century from northeastern Angola and southwestern Republic of Congo.
The Lagos serotine bat (Eptesicus platyops) is known only from a few specimens collected in Nigeria, Senegal, and on Bioko.

The Patagonian chinchilla mouse (Euneomys chinchilloides) is confined to southern Argentina (Tierra del Fuego and neighbouring islands) and southern Chile (Magallanes region), where it is threatened by the overgrazing of its habitat by sheep.
The pungent pipistrelle bat (Falsistrellus mordax) appears to be known only from nineteenth-century historical records from an undefined locality or localities on Java.
Fox's mole rat (Fukomys foxi) is known only from the Jos Plateau of central Nigeria and from another locality in western Cameroon.
The Lunda rope squirrel (Funisciurus bayonii) is known only from southwestern Democratic Republic of Congo and northeastern Angola.
Du Chaillu's striped squirrel (Funisciurus duchaillui) is known only from a small area of central Gabon between the Ogooué River and Massif du Chaillu.
The Somali elephant shrew (Galegeeska revoilii) was historically known only from northern Somalia, where it was last recorded after 1968 and thought to be extinct.
Gerlepp's mouse (Galenomys garleppi) is known only from a few localities across the Andean Plateau, where it was last recorded in 1975.
The king genet (Genetta poensis) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Republic of Congo, Liberia, Ghana, Ivory Coast and the island of Bioko.
The Berbera gerbil (Gerbillus acticola) is known only from a few individuals collected at various elevations in northwestern Somalia.
Glen's wattled bat (Glauconycteris gleni) is known only from two widely-spaced localities (Cameroon and western Uganda).
The Javan thick-thumbed bat (Glischropus javanus) is known only from a few specimens collected nearly seventy years apart on Mount Pangrango.
Behn's big-eared bat (Glyphonycteris behnii) is known only from six specimens collected over a wide area of southwestern Brazil.
The sculptor squirrel (Glyphotes simus) is confined to the mountains of northern Borneo (Sabah and Sarawak, Malaysia).
The arid woodland thicket rat (Grammomys aridulus) is known only from the Marrah Mountains.
The grey-headed thicket rat (Grammomys caniceps) is confined to dry coastal shrubland in eastern Kenya and southeastern Somalia.
Edith's leaf-eared mouse (Graomys edithae) is confined to two areas of montane grassland in northwestern Argentina (Catamarca and La Rioja provinces).
De Winton's African dormouse (Graphiurus angolensis) is known only from a few localities in Angolia and western Zambia.
Johnston's African dormouse (Graphiurus johnstoni) is confined to the savanna woodlands of southern Malawi and possibly adjacent areas of Zambia and Zimbabwe.
The Yunnan bush rat (Hadromys yunnanensis) is known only from a small area of the Yunnan Plateau.
Margaret's ranee mouse (Haeromys margarettae) is known only from two old historical collections from two, widely-separated localities in northern Sabah and southwestern Sarawak.
Peters' tube-nosed bat (Harpiola grisea) is known only from a small area of northern India (Uttarakhand).
The false serotine bat (Hesperoptenus doriae) is known only from a few specimens collected in southern peninsular Malaysia and northwestern Borneo (Sarawak).

Boeadi's roundleaf bat (Hipposideros boeadii) is known only from a few specimens collected from Rawa Aopa Watumohai National Park, on the southeastern peninsula of Sulawesi (Sulawesi Tenggara province).
species.iucn: Hipposideros boeadii Bates, Rossiter, Suyanto & Kingston, 2007

species.e: The Philippine large leaf-nosed bat (Hipposideros coronatus) is known only from a handful of specimens collected throughout the Philippines.
The Timor leaf-nosed bat (Hipposideros crumeniferus) is confined to Timor.

The crested leaf-nosed bat (Hipposideros inexpectatus) is known only from three historical collections in central and northern Sulawesi, the first two in the 1870s and the third at some time prior to 1925.
Husson's water rat (Hydromys hussoni) is known only from the Wissel Lakes area of western New Guinea (Papua province, Indonesia).
The New Britain water rat (Hydromys neobritannicus) is known only from three specimens collected from New Britain during the 1930s, there there are unconfirmed reports as well from Umboi.
Ziegler's water rat (Hydromys ziegleri) is a semi-aquatic species known only from the southern slopes of the Prince Alexander Mountains.
Tate's rice rat (Hylaeamys tatei) is known only from three localities in central Ecuador.
The long-eared gymnure (Hylomys megalotis) is a hedgehog-like mammal known only from limestone karst forests in central Laos (Khammouane province).
Bartels' flying squirrel (Hylopetes bartelsi) is confined to the forests of Mount Pangrango.
Eisentraut's pipistrelle bat (Hypsugo eisentrauti) is likely confined to the montane forests of southwestern Cameroon.
Joffre's pipistrelle bat (Hypsugo joffrei) is known only from a few specimens collected over a wide area in northern and northwestern Myanmar, India, Nepal, and Vietnam.
Stolzmann's crab-eating rat (Ichthyomys stolzmanni) is known only from a few localities spread over a wide area of Ecuador and western Peru.
Barbara Brown's brush-tailed rat (Isothrix barbarabrownae) is known only from a single cloud forest within the Manu Biosphere Reserve in southeastern Peru (Cusco department).
Thaler's jerboa (Jaculus thaleri) is known only from two localities in the Dasht-e-Lut Desert.
The copper woolly bat (Kerivoula cuprosa) is known only from a few scattered records across western and central Africa.
The climbing rock cavy (Kerodon acrobata) is a type of rodent known only from a small area of east-central Brazil (Goiás and Tocantins).
The El Ahuaca viscacha (Lagidium ahuacaense) is a type of rodent confined to rocky habitats on El Ahuaca, where the total population may number only around a few dozen.
species.iucn: Lagidium ahuacaense Ledesma, Wener, Spotorno & Albuja, 2009

species.e: The hairy-tailed bat (Lasiurus ebenus) is known only from two specimens collected in southeastern Brazil (São Paulo).
The groove-toothed forest mouse (Leimacomys buettneri) is known only from two specimens collected in west-central Togo in 1890.
The Pacific coast long-tongued bat (Lonchophylla chocoana) is known only from four localities in northwestern Ecuador and southwestern Colombia.
Kalko's round-eared bat (Lophostoma kalkoae) is known only from a single colony recorded from Soberanía National Park in central Panama (Panamá Oeste province).
The grey brush-furred rat (Lophuromys cinereus) is known only from a few specimens collected at high elevations in Kahuzi-Biéga National Park.
The dusky armoured tree rat (Makalata obscura) is known only from its vague type description.
Anderson's mouse opossum (Marmosa andersoni) is known only from three localities in southern Peru (Cusco department).
Tyler's mouse opossum (Marmosa tyleriana) is known only from three isolated tepuis in Venezuala (Auyán, Marahuaca and Sarisariñama).
The slim-faced slender mouse opposum (Marmosops cracens) is confined to a small area of lowland rainforest in northwestern Venezuela (Falcón state).
Creighton's slender mouse opossum (Marmosops creightoni) is known only from a small area of western Bolivia (La Paz department), where it may be threatened by loss of habitat.
The Sumatran mountain spiny rat (Maxomys hylomyoides) is known only from a few disjunct localities in central-western Sumatra.
The Cuc Phuong ferret-badger (Melogale cucphuongensis) is known only from two specimens collected from a heavily-degraded forest area in northern Vietnam.
species.iucn: Melogale cucphuongensis Nadler, Streicher, Stefen, Schwierz & Roos, 2011

species.e: The Rossel mosaic-tailed rat (Melomys arcium) is known only from a small number of specimens collected in 1956 and 1960.
The Yamdena mosaic-tailed rat (Melomys cooperae) is known only from its original type series collected in 1995.
species.iucn: Melomys cooperae Kitchener in Kitchener & Maryanto, 1995

species.e: The Riama mosaic-tailed rat (Melomys howi) is known only from Riama, but may perhaps occur on other islands within the Tanimbar Archipelago.
species.iucn: Melomys howi Kitchener in Kitchener & Suyanto, 1996

species.e: Zarundny's jird (Meriones zarudnyi) is confined to semi-arid highland areas in northeastern Iran and northern Afghanistan.
The woolly-headed spiny tree rat (Mesomys leniceps) is known only from two small areas of montane cloud forest in northwestern Peru (Amazonas department).

The spade-toothed beaked whale (Mesoplodon traversii) is considered to be the rarest of the beaked whales, and was long known only from a partial jaw found washed ashore on Pitt Island, New Zealand in 1872.
The southern groove-tailed moss-mouse (Microhydromys argenteus) is known only from three localities across a wide area of central and southeastern Papua New Guinea.
The northern groove-toothed moss-mouse (Microhydromys richardsoni) is known only from a small number of specimens collected over a wide area of northern New Guinea.
Burir's big-eared bat (Micronycteris buriri) is known only from Saint Vincent.
species.iucn: Micronycteris buriri Larsen, Siles, Pedersen & Kwiecinski, 2011

species.e: The Anatolian vole (Microtus anatolicus) is confined to an isolated area of steppe in central-western Turkey (Konya province).
The Evoron vole (Microtus evoronensis) is known only from a small area of far southeastern Siberia within the lower Amur River floodplains.
The Kerman vole (Microtus kermanensis) is known only from a few specimens collected in southeastern Iran.
Peterson's long-fingered bat (Miniopterus petersoni) appears to be restricted to the lowland rainforests of the southeast corner of Madagascar (former Toliara province).
species.iucn: Miniopterus petersoni Goodman, Bradman, Maminirina, Ryan, Christidis & Appleton, 2008

species.e: The Yucatán mastiff bat (Molossus alvarezi) is known only from the northern and eastern Yucatán Peninsula.
Trevor's free-tailed bat (Mops trevori) is known only from a few specimens collected over a very wide area of West and Central Africa.
The Sumatran mastiff bat (Mormopterus doriae) is known only from its original description in 1907 from northeastern Sumatra (Sumatera Utara province).
The Sumatran shrewlike mouse (Mus crociduroides) is currently known only from high-elevation montane forest on Mount Kerinci, but may perhaps occur more widely in the Barisan Mountains.
The Sichuan weasel (Mustela russelliana) is known only from three collection records within a small area of north-central China (Sichuan).
The Ethiopian groove-tailed rat (Mylomys rex) is known only from a single skin collected from the Charada Forest in central Ethiopia.
Tate's three-striped dasyure (Myoictis wavicus) is a small, carnivorous marsupial known only from a handful of specimens collected from a small area of eastern Papua New Guinea.
Setzer's mouse-tailed dormouse (Myomimus setzeri) is known only from a few specimens collected in the mountains of eastern Turkey and northwestern Iran.
The Anjouan mouse-eared bat (Myotis anjouanensis) is a little-known species confined to Anjouan.
The Bokhara mouse-eared bat (Myotis bucharensis) is known only from a few specimens collected from three localities in Central Asia (Uzbekistan and Tajikistan).
The Guatemalan mouse-eared bat (Myotis cobanensis) is known only from two specimens collected in the 1950s from central Guatemala (Alta Verapaz department).
Herman's mouse-eared bat (Myotis hermani) is known only from three individuals collected from the Malay Peninsula and Sabang Island north of Sumatra.
The insular mouse-eared bat (Myotis insularum) is known only from a perhaps incorrectly-labeled type specimen, said to have originated from Samoa.
Morris' mouse-eared bat (Myotis morrisi) is known only from two widely-separated localities (northeastern Nigeria and western Ethiopia).
Schaub's mouse-eared bat (Myotis schaubi) is a rare species known only from a few localities within the southern Caucasus Mountains of Armenia, and from the northwestern Zagros Mountains of Iran.
The least big-eared bat (Neonycteris pusilla) is known only from a small area of northwestern Brazil (Amazonas), possibly extending into eastern Colombia.
The Sumatran striped rabbit (Nesolagus netscheri) is confined to disjunct areas of remote montane rainforest in the Barisan Mountains.

The Madagascar slit-faced bat (Nycteris madagascariensis) is known only from two specimens collected in 1910, in the Irodo River Valley of northern Madagascar near Analamera (former Antsiranana province).
Parisi's slit-faced bat (Nycteris parisii) is known only from three specimens collected from southern Somalia, southern Ethiopia and northern Cameroon.
Vinson's slit-faced bat (Nycteris vinsoni) is known only from two specimens smoked out of a baobab tree in the mid 1960s in southern Mozambique.
The round-eared tube-nosed fruit bat (Nyctimene cyclotis) is known only from the Arfak Mountains and Mansuar Island in northwestern New Guinea (Papua Barat province, Indonesia).
The demonic tube-nosed fruit bat (Nyctimene masalai) appears to be confined to New Ireland.
The greedy Olalla rat (Olallamys edax) is known only from a single high-altitude locality in Barinas state.

species.s: Scattered patches of lowland dry forest
species.e: The Oaxacan pocket gopher (Orthogeomys cuniculus) is confined to a few localities on the Isthmus of Tehuantepec of southern Mexico (Oaxaca).

The four-toed rice tenrec (Oryzorictes tetradactylus) is a semi-fossorial species that appears to be restricted to the south-central highlands and the flank of the Eastern Escarpment (former Fianarantsoa province).
The Javan mastiff bat (Otomops formosus) is known only from four specimens collected in 1939 and in 1990 from western Java (Banten and Jawa Barat provinces).
The Papuan mastiff bat (Otomops papuensis) is known only from a handful of specimens collected from two disjunct localities in southeastern Papua New Guinea.
The mantled mastiff bat (Otomops secundus) is known only from six specimens collected from three localities in Papua New Guinea.
The short-haired water rat (Paraleptomys wilhelmina) is known only from three, widely-separated localities in the Central Highlands of New Guinea.
Stein's mosaic-tailed rat (Paramelomys steini) is known only from six specimens collected from Mount Weyland.
The yellow-spotted tree rat (Pattonomys flavidus) is known only from two localities on Margarita Island.
The bare-tailed armoured tree rat (Pattonomys occasius) is known only from a few specimens collected from the western Amazon in eastern Ecuador and northern Peru.
Hopkins' groove-toothed swamp rat (Pelomys hopkinsi) is confined to swampy areas between Lake Victoria and the Albertine Rift Valley.
The Selangor pygmy flying squirrel (Petaurillus kinlochii) is known only from a few specimens collected in southwestern peninsular Malaysia.
Olrog's four-eyed opossum (Philander olrogi) is known only from two localities in central Bolivia (Beni and Santa Cruz departments).
Osgood's leaf-eared mouse (Phyllotis osgoodi) is known only from a small area of northern Chile (Arica y Pinacota region).
Heller's pipistrelle bat (Pipistrellus aero) is known only from a few disjunct localities in central Kenya and possibly northwestern Ethiopia.

Racey's pipistrelle bat (Pipistrellus raceyi) is known only from a few specimens collected at two lowland rainforest localities in the central-east and two more, lowland dry forest sites in the central-west.
species.iucn: Pipistrellus raceyi Bates, Ratrimomanarivo, Harrison & Goodman, 2006

species.e: The Malaysian tree rat (Pithecheir parvus) is confined to southern peninsular Malaysia (Pahang and Johore states).
The Darién broad-nosed bat (Platyrrhinus aquilus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Darién and Pirre ranges of eastern Panama and northwestern Colombia.
The Ethiopian long-eared bat (Plecotus balensis) is known only from a few localities within the Ethiopian Highlands.
Christie's long-eared bat (Plecotus christii) is known only from a few localities in northeastern Africa, including Egypt, eastern Libya, and Sudan.
Champion's tree mouse (Pogonomys championi) is known only from the Telefomin and Tifalmin valleys of west-central Papua New Guinea.
Dollman's tree mouse (Prionomys batesi) is known only from a few specimens collected from south-central Cameroon, southwestern Central African Republic, and northwestern Republic of Congo.
The Minca spiny rat (Proechimys mincae) is confined to a small area of Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta.
The Liangshan vole (Proedromys liangshanensis) is known only from two nature reserves in southwestern Sichuan.
species.iucn: Proedromys liangshanensis Liu, Sun, Zeng & Zhao, 2007

species.e: German's one-toothed moss-mouse (Pseudohydromys germani) is known only from the Owen Stanley Mountains.
The western moss-mouse (Pseudohydromys occidentalis) is known only from two disjunct areas in the Central Highlands.

The khting-vor (Pseudonovibos spiralis) is a mysterious bovid reputed to exist in Cambodia and Vietnam, and known only from a few curiously-twisted horns that may perhaps be nothing more than artificially-crafted cattle horns for use as talismans.
The Myanmar flying fox (Pteropus intermedius) is known only from two roosting colonies in northern peninsular Myanmar.
The Kai flying fox (Pteropus keyensis) is confined to the Kai Islands.
The Okinawa flying fox (Pteropus loochoensis) is known only from three specimens of unknown provenance, but is thought to have been collected on Okinawa during the nineteenth century.
The Vogelkop mountain rat (Rattus arfakiensis) is known only from specimens collected in the Arfak Nature Reserve in the 1930s.
The Aceh rat (Rattus blangorum) is known only from two specimens collected in the foothills of the Leuser Range.
The Kerinci rat (Rattus korinchi) is known only from two specimens collected from Mount Kerinci and Mount Talakmau in central-western Sumatra during the early twentieth century.
The Tawi-Tawi forest rat (Rattus tawitawiensis) is known only from three specimens collected on Tawi-Tawi in 1971.
The convex horseshoe bat (Rhinolophus convexus) is known only from a few specimens collected in the Cameron Highlands.
The Cauca climbing mouse (Rhipidomys caucensis) is known only from twelve specimens collected over a relatively wide area of the Cordillera Occidental and Cordillera Central of northwestern Colombia.
The Tapulao shrew-rat (Rhynchomys tapulao) is known only from Mount Tapulao.
species.iucn: Rhynchomys tapulao Balete, Rickart, Rosell-Ambal, Jansa & Heaney, 2007

species.e: The Linduan rousette fruit bat (Rousettus linduensis) is known only from four specimens collected in Lore Lindu National Park, west-central Sulawesi (Sulawesi Tengah province).
The delicate salt flat mouse (Salinomys delicatus) is confined to a few isolated populations in northwestern Argentina (Catamarca, La Rioja, San Juan, Mendoza and San Luis provinces).
The Kharan pygmy jerboa (Salpingotulus michaelis) is known only from the Kharan Desert.
Heptner's pygmy jerboa (Salpingotus heptneri) is confined to the Kyzylkum Desert, where it is known only from a few specimens.
The pallid pygmy jerboa (Salpingotus pallidus) is confined to a few localities in central and eastern Kazakhstan.
Paulina's limestone rat (Saxatilomys paulinae) is known only from specimens collected within the Khammouane Limestone NBCA in central Laos and from north-central Vietnam (Quang Binh province).
species.iucn: Saxatilomys paulinae Musser, Smith, Robinson & Lunde, 2005

species.e: The fiery squirrel (Sciurus flammifer) is confined to a small area of north-central Venezuela (Bolívar state), where it is threatened by loss of habitat.
Sanborn's squirrel (Sciurus sanborni) is known only from a few specimens collected in southeastern Peru (Madre de Dios department).
Robbins' house bat (Scotophilus nucella) is known only from southeastern Ivory Coast, southern Ghana, western Uganda and northeastern Tanzania.

The western yellow bat (Scotophilus tandrefana) is similarly known only from two specimens, one from near Parc National Tsingy de Bemaraha and the second at Sarodrano (former Mahajanga and Toliara provinces).
The desert dormouse (Selevinia betpakdalaensis) is a rare species known only from a few localities over a relatively wide area of central Kazakhstan.
The Glacier Bay water shrew (Sorex alaskanus) is confined to a small area of southern coastal Alaska.
The New Mexico shrew (Sorex neomexicanus) appears to be confined to Capitan, Manzano and Sandia mountains in south-central New Mexico.
The dusky shrew (Sorex sinalis) is known only from a few mountaintop localities spread over a relatively wide area of central China (Gansu, Sichuan and Shaanxi).
Jackson's fat mouse (Steatomys jacksoni) is known only from two localities (west-central Ghana and southwestern Nigeria).
Rupp's mouse (Stenocephalemys ruppi) is confined to the Gughe Mountains.
The La Perla yellow-shouldered bat (Sturnira perla) is known only from a small area of northwestern Ecuador, where it is threatened by loss of habitat.
The Palawan montane squirrel (Sundasciurus rabori) is restricted to a few pockets of montane forest, where it is known from only a few specimens.
The Mount Kenya mole shrew (Surdisorex polulus) is known only from two or three specimens collected on Mount Kenya.
The Venezuelan lowland cottontail rabbit (Sylvilagus varynaensis) is known only from a few localities in northwestern Venezuela (Barinas, Portuguesa, and Guárico states).
The lesser forest shrew (Sylvisorex oriundus) is known only from two localities in northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The Bamenda forest shrew (Sylvisorex silvanorum) is known only from a few specimens collected from the Western High Plateau.
Bang's mountain squirrel (Syntheosciurus brochus) is a poorly-known species confined to a few localities within the Isthmian Highlands.
Hamilton's tomb bat (Taphozous hamiltoni) is known only from a very few records, mainly in east-central Africa (Sudan, Somalia, Kenya, and Tanzania), with an additional report from southern Chad.

Shepherd's beaked whale (Tasmacetus shepherdi) is known only from a small number of at-sea sightings and a few dozen strandings in the temperate waters of New Zealand, Argentina, Tristan da Cunha, Australia, and the Juan Fernández Islands.
Schouteden's thicket rat (Thamnomys schoutedeni) is known only from two, widely-separated localities in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Tate's fat-tailed mouse opposum (Thylamys tatei) is confined to a few localities in the coastal deserts and shrublands of western Peru (Ancash and Lima departments).
LaVal's disk-winged bat (Thyroptera lavali) is known only from a few specimens collected over a relatively wide area of northwestern South America.
Daovantien's limestone rat (Tonkinomys daovantieni) is known only from the Huu Lien Nature Reserve in northeastern Vietnam (Lang Son province).
The Peruvian tree rat (Toromys rhipidurus) is known only from a few specimens collected from northern Peru (Loreto department).
The dark-caped Atlantic spiny rat (Trinomys mirapitanga) is known only from a few specimens collected from two localities in coastal eastern Brazil (Bahia).
The Luzon short-nosed rat (Tryphomys adustus) is confined to a few localities in central and northern Luzon (Benguet, Laguna and Tarlac provinces).
The striped tree shrew (Tupaia dorsalis) is widely distributed within the rainforests of north-central Borneo, but is still known only from a few specimens and appears to be everywhere rare.
Kirchner's viscacha rat (Tympanoctomys kirchnerorum) is known only from a small area of south-central Argentina (Chubut province).
species.iucn: Tympanoctomys kirchnerorum Teta, Pardiñas, Sauthier & Gallardo, 2014

species.e: The Great Kai giant naked-tailed rat (Uromys siebersi) is confined to Great Kai Island.
Viera's long-tonged bat (Xeronycteris vieirai) is known only from a few localities in northeastern Brazil (Paraíba, Ceara, Pernambuco, Alagoas and Bahia).
The Taiwanese hagfish (Eptatretus chinensis) is an eel-like species confined to the South China Sea, where it is directly harvested for food.
The goliath hagfish (Eptatretus goliath) is an eel-like species known only from Hauraki Canyon off New Zealand.

Lophelia's hagfish (Eptatretus lopheliae) is an eel-like species known only from a few specimens collected and observed in the western Atlantic off the southeastern United States (North Carolina and South Carolina).
The Gulf of Mexico hagfish (Eptatretus minor) is an eel-like species confined to the northern Gulf of Mexico, where it is potentially threatened by shrimp and scallop trawling.
Strahan's hagfish (Eptatretus strahani) is an eel-like species known only from seven specimens collected in the northern Philippines and along the western coast of Australia.
The Magellan hagfish (Myxine debueni) is known only from two specimens collected in the Strait of Magellan.
The bootlace hagfish (Nemamyxine elongata) is a freshwater and marine species known only from two museum specimens collected from New Zealand.
The Argentine hagfish (Notomyxine tridentiger) is confined to the southern coast of South America from eastern Argentina to southern Chile, where it was last recorded in 1968.
Reid's arboreal alligator lizard (Abronia reidi) is known only from a couple of specimens collected from San Martín Tuxtlas Volcano.

Bouet's spiny-toed lizard (Acanthodactylus boueti) is known only from a few specimens collected over a relatively wide area of West Africa (southwestern Ghana, northern Togo, central Benin, and west-central Nigeria).
The Kunua blind snake (Acutotyphlops kunuaensis) is a little-known fossorial species confined to lowland forests.
Fox's mountain meadow snake (Adelophis foxi) is known only from a small area of relictural montane pine forest in southwestern Durango, where it was last collected in 1981.
The Somali snake (Aeluroglena cucullata) is known only from five specimens collected from northern Somalia.
The Rondo worm snake (Afrotyphlops rondoensis) is confined to the Rondo and Makonde plateaus of extreme southeastern Tanzania.
